headings.text: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS

preamble.header: Persons with Disabilities (Accessibility) Regulations, 2023 — enacting formula
preamble.text: S. I. No. 51 of 2023 DISCRIMINATION AGAINST PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES (PROHIBITION) ACT, NO 2, 2018 PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES (ACCESSIBILITY) REGULATIONS, 2023 [22nd day of May, 2023] Commence- ment. In exercise of the powers conferred on it by section 56 of the Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act, 2018 (“the Act”) and all other powers enabling it in that behalf, the Governing Council of the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities (“the Commission”), makes the following Regulations —

regs.title: Objectives.
regs.text: 1. The objectives of these Regulations are to— (a) ensure effective collaboration with relevant agencies towards ensuring ensuring easy and unimpeded access to services in the Nigerian built environment by persons with disabilities ; (b) provide specifications for policy makers, regulators, implementers, and service providers to ensure quality and non-discriminatory services in the Nigerian built environment ; (c) provide standards and codes for the design and construction of an accessible built environment, including roads, and transportation facilities ; (d) provide a tool for measuring or auditing universal accessibility in the built environment ; (e) guide developers, designers and other persons involved in the built environment process in incorporating accessibility principles in the planning, design, and execution stages of building work ; and (f ) increase awareness on accessibility standards and the need for a barrier- free design in the built environment.

regs.title: Application.
regs.text: 2. These Regulations shall apply to— (a) Ministries, Departments, and Agencies of Government (MDAs) ; (b) international organisations, and non-governmental organisations ; (c) structures and facilities accessible to members of the public, and their owners ; and (d) persons undertaking any activity in relation to built environment, including audit teams, facility managers, public officials, architects, engineers, and developers.

regs.title: Bridges with pedestrian access.
regs.text: 3. —(1) A person involved in built environment shall ensure that pedestrian routes are— (a) safe and easy to use by persons with disabilities ; and (b) easily identifiable, clearly separated from vehicular routes, and free of obstacles at all times. (2) In the case of a bridge with pedestrian access— (a) pedestrian sidewalks located on either side of the bridges shall have— (i) a slope not greater than 1 : 20 to the ground level, and (ii) where practicable, a cross slope not greater than 1 : 50 to the ground level ; (b) sidewalk on the bridge shall be a minimum width of – (i) 1220 mm, where minimal pedestrian traffic is expected, or (ii) 1800mm, where a high pedestrian traffic is expected ; (c) handrails or guards located beside sidewalks shall be – (i) easy to grasp, (ii) a maximum width of 50mm, and (iii) mounted at a suitable height, as specified in Figure 1.008 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; and (d) pedestrian footbridges shall, where practicable, have ramp options rather than stairways only.

regs.title: Zebra crossing or crosswalks.
regs.text: 4. —(1) A zebra crossing or crosswalk at a roadway intersection shall— (a) be located — (i) to ensure that the sidewalk and the zebra crossing or crosswalk are at right angles to one another, (ii) to ensure a clear view of traffic in each direction, and (iii) at sufficient distance of 20,000 mm from the intersection to permit a safe crossing ; (b) include appropriate kerb ramps at each end ; and (c) be free of obstacles, such as light stands, traffic signal supports, boxes, or waste containers. (2) A zebra crossing or crosswalk shall — (a) have kerb ramps at the end of a walkway, where sidewalks are provided, or where level differences exceeding 19mm occur, as specified in Figure 1.001 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; (b) be of a minimum width of 3,000mm, and clearly marked by 100 mm, painted white lines or by using distinctive, highly contrasting paving materials ; and (c) have tactile paving. (3) An intermediate traffic island shall — (a) include kerb ramps ; (b) be leveled to street paving ; and (c) be clearly marked by white lines or distinctive highly contrasting paving. (4) Where a traffic light or pedestrian crossover is provided at zebra crossing or crosswalk — (a) a clearly identifiable pedestrian pushbutton shall be located adjacent to the zebra crossing or crosswalk and mounted on a nearby post at a height of 1065mm ; and (b) paving shall be level at posts, providing a minimum of 915mm x 1220mm clear approach area for pedestrians, as specified in Figure 1.002 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Kerb ramps or kerb cuts on public right of way.
regs.header: 5. Kerb ramps or kerb cuts on public right of way.
regs.arrangement_title: Kerb ramps or kerb cuts on public right of way
regs.text: 5. —(1) A kerb ramp shall be provided, where there is a level difference between a sidewalk or pedestrian pathway and the road surface, including where a pedestrian zebra crossing or crosswalk is provided, as specified in Figure 1.003 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) A kerb ramp transition slope shall be of a minimum length of 1500mm, as specified in Figure 1.004 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) The minimum width of the kerb ramp shall be 900mm between two flared sides of a minimum width of 1200mm. (4) A kerb ramp shall — (a) have a minimum slope at a ratio of 1 :20 for a short kerb, and a maximum slope of the flare at 1 : 10 ; and (b) be made of non-slippery materials, with contrasted colours. (5) A kerb ramp or kerb cut shall have tactile markings, and be provided on both sides of a zebra or pedestrian crossing, particularly where catch basin is necessary. (6) A kerb ramp shall — (a) have a minimum width of 1500mm, where the ramp is located on a public thoroughfare, as specified in Figure 1.003 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; (b) have flared, non-slip sides, and be clearly different from the surrounding sidewalk and at right angles to the path of travel, as specified See Figure 1.005 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; (c) have at its lower edge, a cane detectable rounded edge of 13mm in height ; (d) have at its top, a level landing with a minimum depth of 1065mm, as specified in Figure 1.004 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; (e) be of a different textured material, as specified in Figure 1.005 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; and (f ) be free from accumulated rainwater, and contain no manhole, storm gratings, or other obstacles.

regs.title: Grades and elevation changes.
regs.text: 6. —(1) A grade on a road and sidewalk shall be designed and constructed to ensure that the slope of pedestrian route does not exceed 1:20. (2) An accessible path of travel shall have kerb cuts to keep the sidewalk as level as possible. (3) A ramp shall be provided, where an elevation change exceeding 1:20 is necessary, or where steps are unavoidable. (4) Where a sloped landscaped area exceeding 3:1 is located adjacent to a pedestrian route, a clear boundary edge, such as an up-stand kerb or retaining wall with a minimum height of 150mm shall be provided, as specified in Figures 1.06 and 1.007 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Where a grade drop-off adjacent to the sidewalk is 460mm or more, a handrail or guard shall be provided, as specified in Figure 1.007 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Guards and handrails (general).
regs.text: 7. —(1) There shall be continuous handrails on both sides of a ramp or stairs, including where three or more staircases are provided. (2) A handrail shall — (a) be easy to grip ; (b) be made preferably of metal or any other approved strong and sturdy material ; (c) not be too smooth or having spikes or sharp edges ; (d) not exceed 50mm in diameter ; and (e) be mounted between 865mm and 965mm, above stair nosing, as specified in Figures 1.008 and 1.009 First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) The distance between a handrail and a vertical wall surface shall be a minimum width of 40mm, and handrails shall continue unbroken along the stairs and on the landing area. (4) A level section of the handrail shall extend to minimum length of 300mm beyond the top and bottom risers of a flight of stairs or ramps, as specified in Figure 1.010 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) A handrail on the inside curve of stairs or ramps shall not extend beyond 100mm. (6) The end of a handrail shall terminate by turning down or by going into the wall. (7) A guard shall be put in place on both sides of a ramp, where height difference is sizable. (8) A guard or handrail provided on a terrace or viewing platform shall be designed to ensure that a seated person can see under the handrail or guard. (9) A guard or handrail shall not be located within 1000mm of a roadway. (10) A handrail shall measure at a height of — (a) 600mm — 700mm from the ground level for use of by children and wheelchair users ; and (b) 800mm — 900mm for use by other users. (11) In order to prevent wheels from falling out of the ramp edge, rails for the wheels shall be placed at a height of 150mm-200mm, at the bottom of the railing. (12) Where the width of a ramp exceeds a width off 3,000mm, handrails located along the ramp shall be painted in contrasting colours and where stairs exceed 2,700mm, an intermediate handrail with a minimum width of 1500mm shall be provided on one side of the stairs.

regs.title: Vertical clearance.
regs.text: 8. —(1) A minimum vertical clearance of 2030mm shall be allowed, for external and internal walkways. (2) Where vertical clearance is less than 2030mm, a guardrail or other barriers shall be provided. (3) The leading edge of a guardrail or barrier provided pursuant to sub- regulation (2) of this regulation shall be positioned at least 685mm above the finished floor or ground, as specified in Figure 1.012 in the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Paving surfaces at the top and bottom of a flights of stairs or steps shall include a cane detectable and textured walking surface measuring a minimum width of 915mm, forward of the first riser, and continuous from the top of the stair, as an early warning of an impending level change to persons with visual disabilities, as specified in Figure 1.025 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Exterior doors that open onto landings shall be avoided, where possible, in order to minimize hazards, and where such doors are unavoidable, the landing width shall be increased to 1670mm, provided that no door shall open onto any sloping section of a ramp.

regs.title: Lay-bys for vehicles (Passenger loading zones).
regs.text: 9. —(1) A special lay-by area, free of other vehicular traffic shall be provided at bus stops, train stations and other similar places, as specified in Figure 1.013 in the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) A lay-by space shall — (a) be located within 30000mm of a main or other accessible entrance ; (b) be leveled with a minimum width of 3050mm and length of 7925mm, and (c) have a kerb cut located towards the rear of the space. (3) A lay-by shall have headroom with a minimum clearance of 3555mm for special transit vehicles and adapted vans, as specified in Figure 1.013 in the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) A sidewalk adjacent to lay-by headroom shall have a minimum clearance of 1980mm width, to accommodate side-loading vehicles with hydraulic lifts or cranes. (5) Where a shelter is provided at a bus stop— (a) the bus stop pad may be located within or outside of the shelter ; and (b) the shelter shall — (i) have a clear floor or ground space measuring a minimum length of 2,440mm and minimum width of 1525mm, and (ii) be connected by an accessible route to a boarding and alighting area. (6) A bus stop boarding and alighting area shall have a— (a) firm and stable surface ; and (b) clear minimum length of 2440mm, measured perpendicular to the curb or vehicle roadway edge, and a clear minimum width of 1525mm, measured parallel to the vehicle roadway. (7) A vehicle boarding and alighting area shall be connected to a street, sidewalk, or walkway by an accessible route. (8) The slope of a bus stop boarding and alighting area— (a) parallel to the roadway, shall be the same as the roadway, to the maximum extent practicable ; and (b) perpendicular to the roadway, shall not be steeper than 1:48. (9) Kerb ramps shall be provided at passenger pick-up points, where the difference in road pavement and sidewalk levels are greater than 19mm. (10) Van parking spaces at passenger pick-up points shall be a minimum of 7315mm in length by 2590mm in width, as specified in Figure 1.032 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (11) A designated passenger pick-up point shall have a sidewalk or safe pedestrian zone, located behind the vehicle and at the passenger boarding side of the vehicle, a minimum of 2000mm wide in length or width of the boarding space, to ensure safe loading or boarding and unloading or alighting. (12) A designated passenger pick-up point shall be marked with an internationally recognized symbol of accessibility.

regs.title: Paths, sidewalks and walkways.
regs.text: 10. —(1) An entrance path or sidewalk in a public right of way or walkways shall be made of firm, level, and non-slip materials, and of a minimum width of 1800mm such as to allow atleast two wheelchairs pass one another, where two- way traffic is expected. (2) A sidewalk shall not exceed a maximum gradient of 1:20, where it exceeds the maximum gradient, it shall be considered a ramp of which handrails shall be installed, except where it is prevented by site conditions, as specified in Figure 1.027 in the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) A walkway or path around a residential environment shall be a minimum of 1100mm, and widened to a width of 1675mm at 30000mm intervals to accommodate persons using mobility aids. (4) Unit paving materials used in sidewalks, paths and walkways shall have joints with a maximum width of 6mm, as specified in Figure 1.016 and 1.025 in the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Where grating is to be located on sidewalks, opening in the grating shall be of a maximum width of 13mm, and bars of grating shall be perpendicular to the path of travel, as specified in Figure 1.017 in the First Schedule to these Regulations. (6) Clearly marked continuous amenity strips shall be used at the edge of a sidewalk to accommodate freestanding objects and other amenities. (7) The strips referred to in sub-regulation (6) of this regulation shall — (a) be of a minimum width of 610mm ; and (b) separated from a pedestrian walkway by a contrasting colour ; and (c) cane detectable border that is a minimum width of 305mm, as specified in Figure 1.006 in the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Pedestrian route.
regs.text: 11. —(1) A pedestrian route shall be a minimum width of 1500mm. (2) A pedestrian route shall be free of protruding obstacles, overhanging signs, or any other obstacle in the walking area, as specified in Figures 1.006, 1.07 and 1.018 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) The maximum allowable protrusion of objects into a pedestrian route shall be 100mm from grade to a height of 685mm from the floor.

regs.title: Ramps.
regs.text: 12. —(1) A ramp shall be provided, where gradient is more than 1:20. (2) A ramp provided under sub-regulation (1) of this regulation shall comply with the criteria specified in regulation 6 of these Regulations.

regs.title: Ramps with mounted handrails.
regs.text: 13. —(1) Ramp with mounted handrail shall be of a maximum width of 1100mm, and a minimum of 1015mm between handrails. (2) For intermediate level landings, a minimum depth of 1670mm by the same width of the ramp shall be provided, and level landings at the top and bottom of the ramp shall be a minimum of 1670mm by 1670mm, as specified in Figures 1.021and 1.024 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) Where a ramp returns upon itself, or a door opens out onto a ramp, the level platform area shall measure a minimum length of 1,670mm and minimum width of 1,670mm, and an additional distance of 600mm for a door opening onto the landing, as specified in Figures 1.022 and 1.023 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) A ramp with slope between 1:20 and 1:12 shall have handrails on both sides, provided that a ramp with a gradient higher than 1:12 shall not be erected in a public building.

regs.title: Tactile marking.
regs.text: 14. A tactile marking of 900mm width with contrasted colours shall be placed at the beginning and end of the ramp, which serve to alert a person with visual disability about the length and width of the ramp.

regs.title: Stairs and steps.
regs.text: 15. —(1) Steps or stairs shall — (a) have uniform closed vertical risers with a height between 100mm and 180mm ; (b) not have open risers ; (c) have uniform horizontal treads with depth between 280mm and 425mm ; (d) have handrails as specified in regulation 16 of these Regulations ; and (e) be at least 1200mm wide. (2) Stairs or steps with nosing at the edge of each tread shall be a maximum length of 25mm. (3) The edges of a step or stair shall be of a contrasting colour, and be made from anti-slip material. (4) The landing at the top and bottom of the stairs shall — (a) measure a minimum length of 1200mm and a minimum width of 1200mm ; and (b) be clear of any door swings or other obstructions. (5) Tactile warning blocks shall be installed at the landing of each flight of stairs, top and bottom.

regs.title: Handrails on stairs.
regs.text: 16. —(1) Where stairs exceed a width of 3000mm, a handrail shall be installed in the centre. (2) Where stairs having vertical clearance has space underneath, it shall comply with the provisions of regulation 8 of these Regulations. (3) Outdoor steps shall be of a firm, non-slip material with a recommended maximum rise of 180mm and a maximum tread length of 300mm, as specified in Figure 1.047 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) The provisions of regulation 7 of these Regulations shall apply to this regulation. (5) Tread nosing shall be clearly marked with either a brightly painted non- slip finish or include an integrated non-slip nosing that clearly contrasts in tone or colour from the tread. (6) Continuous handrails shall be provided on both sides of outdoor flights of stairs or steps, including where three or more steps staircases are provided. (7) Where a flight of stairs or steps is of a width of 2200mm or more, an intermediate handrail shall be installed.

regs.title: Traffic islands (median) on public right of way.
regs.header: 17. Traffic islands (median) on public right of way.
regs.arrangement_title: Traffic islands (median) on public right of way
regs.text: 17. —(1) A traffic island shall be built of materials and finishes that are easily distinguishable from the surrounding paving. (2) A pedestrian zebra crossing or crosswalk that crosses a traffic island shall be level with the main crossing or have kerb ramps for persons using mobility aids. (3) A traffic island shall be of a minimum width of 1500mm, as specified in Figure 1.026 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Where the crossing surface at a traffic island is level with the paving, the safe waiting area of the traffic island shall be made clearly identifiable by using different materials, contrasting colours, or textures that are detectable by persons with visual disability.

regs.title: Drainage gratings.
regs.text: 18. —(1) Drainage gratings shall be positioned beyond the boundaries of the access route. (2) Where gratings are necessary along an access-route, they shall be set to flush with the surrounding surface. (3) Slots in gratings shall be of a maximum width of 13mm, and set at right angles to the dominant line of travel. (4) The diameter of circular holes in gratings shall not exceed 18mm. (5) Dished channels shall not be incorporated within an access route.

regs.title: Accessible routes to entrances.
regs.text: 19. —(1) A pedestrian route to a main entrance or other accessible entrance to a building and other components of public transportation systems, including buses, taxis, ambulances and trains shall be designed to provide a safe, direct, level and obstacle-free path of travel. (2) Accessible route of a minimum width of 1200mm, and made from a firm nonslip material shall be provided at the site boundary to the main entrance or other accessible entrance. (3) Accessible pedestrian routes to an entrance shall not be designed to cross into a vehicular route. (4) Where an accessible pedestrian route crosses into a vehicular route, crossings with kerb ramps marked with a bright contrasting colour or white lines, or a distinct paving shall be provided. (5) A slope on a walkway shall not exceed 1 :20, provided that where steeper walks are necessary, nearby stairs shall be provided and the slopes shall be treated as ramps, as specified in Figure 1.027 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (6) Where the length of an accessible route to accessible entrance exceeds 30000mm, a rest area may, where practicable, be provided at intervals of 30000mm. (7) A rest area of a minimum width of 1200mm fitted with or having space for furniture shall be located to one side of the walkway.

regs.title: Bus or public transit shelters.
regs.text: 20. —(1) A bus or public transit shelter shall be — (a) located on a firm and level base of 4265mm x 1830mm ; and (b) at the same elevation as the sidewalk or walkway. (2) Clearances around a shelter, including clearance on the side of a landing pad, shall measure a minimum width of 1100mm to allow for easy access by pedestrians as specified in Figure 1.028 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) A bus or public transit shelter shall be designed to provide a clear view of on-coming traffic, and have a minimum interior length of 2185mm to accommodate persons using mobility aids. (4) A bus or public transit shelter shall have — (a) a minimum of one seat measuring between 405mm and 460mm high ; (b) a resting ledge, or handrail mounted at a height of 760mm to 815mm ; (c) provide a minimum clear floor or ground space entirely within the shelter in compliance with these Regulations ; and (d) be connected by an accessible route to a boarding and alighting area in compliance with these Regulations. (5) A glazed panel forming part of a bus shelter shall have 50mm diameter stickers or a continuous coloured line, mounted at a maximum height of 1500mm from centre to centre apart.

regs.title: Bus stops.
regs.text: 21. —(1) A waiting area at bus stop shall be — (a) constructed using firm materials ; (b) on a level of minimum of 2000mm width by 12000mm length ; and (c) incorporate seating or a shelter. (2) A bus stop area shall be free from hawking and freestanding objects. (3) The boarding point of a bus stop shall be sizeably spacious to— (a) facilitate disembarkation from the centre door of a bus ; (b) provide for buses to stand at the stop ; and (c) provide additional standing space for intending passengers. (4) Pursuant to sub-regulation (1) of this regulation, where an adjacent footpath is not wide enough to provide an access path between boarding or disembarkation points, a bus stop shall incorporate an access path measuring a minimum width of 1200mm, as specified in Figure 1.029 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Rail Platforms.
regs.text: 22. —(1) A boarding and alighting area shall be connected to a street, sidewalk, or pedestrian paths by an accessible route. (2) A rail platform — (a) shall not exceed a slope of 1 :48 in all directions, (b) have firm non-slippery surface ; and (c) be of the same level to the door of the train. (3) Notwithstanding the provisions of sub-regulation (2)(c) of this regulation, where a platform is not of the same level to the door of the train, a zigzag lift or a transfer platform shall be provided for the use of persons with physical disabilities. (4) Where a rail platform serves coaches operating on existing track or track laid in existing roadway, the slope of the platform parallel to the track shall be permitted to be equal to the slope of the roadway or existing track. (5) A platform boarding edges that is not protected by a platform screen or guard shall have detectable warnings along the full length of the platform. (6) A coach that is boarded from a sidewalk or street-level shall have a low- level platform measured at a minimum height of 205 mm.

regs.title: Emergency routes.
regs.text: 23. Vehicular routes, used by emergency vehicles, including fire trucks and ambulances, shall be clearly identified by a relevant signage, and not cross nor intersect with a primary pedestrian route to a main entrance or other accessible entrance.

regs.title: Parking.
regs.text: 24. —(1) The surface of a car park shall be flat, firm, and non-slippery. (2) A parking space reserved for persons with disabilities shall be provided within 30,000mm to the entrance of the building, and measure a minimum of 2,500mm x 5,000mm. (3) An access area measuring a width of 1,200mm and clearly marked with contrasted colours shall be reserved on the side and at the rear of designated parking spaces, as specified in figure 1.029, 1.030, 1.031 and 1.032 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Where the location for reserved parking space is not close to the building entrance, a covered footway or seats shall be provided at intervals along the accessible route. (5) A vertical sign indicating an accessible parking space reserved for persons with disabilities shall be positioned at a height of 2000mm. (6) An internationally recognized symbol of accessibility shall be painted on the ground within the accessible parking spaces. (7) Where payment is required for parking, an audio function enabled ticket vending machine shall, be provided. (8) For every 100 accessible parking spaces, a minimum of 8 spaces shall be reserved for persons with disabilities, provided that, where the number of parking spaces is less than 25, a minimum of two accessible parking spaces shall be provided. (9) For every 100 accessible parking spaces, a minimum of one space measuring a minimum of 3660mm wide and 5385mm long, shall be reserved for a wheelchair van, as specified in Figure 1.032 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (10) Where space permits, at least one large designated parking space of 4800mm wide x 8000mm long, shall be provided to cater for commercial vehicles converted for side or rear access using hoists or ramps. (11) A headroom clearance for van parking spaces shall be a minimum height of 2750mm. (12) Walkway from a reserved parking to an accessible entrance into a building shall be a minimum width of 1200mm, firm, level, made of non-slip material, and have a texture contrasted with the adjacent surfaces. (13) Where covered or underground parking space is provided, access and exit routes, including ramps serving such spaces, shall have a clear headroom of 2285mm below beams, pipes, or sprinkler heads. (14) A suitable kerb ramp from the accessible car parking area shall be provided where the elevation differential is greater than 13mm. (15) A parking lot and an access route from a lot to a building entrance shall be equipped with artificial lighting measuring 20 lumens per square-meter, and 100 lumens per square-meter on ramps or steps.

regs.title: Garages and enclosed parking spaces.
regs.text: 25. —(1) A garage or enclosed parking space in a public build environment shall — (a) be leveled, and be on the same level as the entrance to a building or the main access route to and from the car park ; (b) permit the use of a wheelchair hoist ; and (c) have a vertical clearance of a minimum height of 2600mm. (2) Without prejudice to sub-regulation (1) of this regulation, where it is not practicable to have a reserved parking space on the same level as an entrance into a building or main access route, a passenger lift or ramp shall be provided to link the different levels of the car park. (3) Where a power-operated door is fitted at the entrance of a garage or enclosed parking space, it shall be capable of being operated from inside a vehicle. (4) The dimensions of a garage or enclosed parking space reserved for a wheelchair user shall be as specified in Figure 1.032 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Clear space or ground space around facilities.
regs.header: 26. Clear space or ground space around facilities.
regs.arrangement_title: Clear space or ground space around facilities
regs.text: 26. —(1) Clear floor or ground space shall be a minimum length of 760mm and a minimum width of 1220mm. (2) Unless otherwise specified, clear floor or ground space shall be — (a) permitted to include knee and toe clearance for a wheelchair user ; and (b) positioned for either forward or parallel approach to an element, as specified in Figure 1.034 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) A full unobstructed side of the clear floor or ground space shall adjoin an accessible route or adjoin another clear floor or ground space. (4) Where a clear floor or ground space is located in an alcove or otherwise confined on all or part of three sides, additional maneuvering clearance shall be provided as specified in Figures 1.034 and 1.035 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) An alcove shall have a — (a) minimum width of 915mm, where its receded depth exceeds 610mm ; or (b) minimum width of 1525mm where its receded depth exceeds 380mm.

regs.title: Road Drainage
regs.text: 27. Road drainage shall be as specified in regulation 18 of these Regulations.

regs.title: Signage (general)
regs.text: 28. —(1) A signage shall be— (a) readable, legible and, where practicable, audible ; (b) illuminated and easy to locate ; and (c) made of robust materials that are easy to change, clean and repair. (2) A visual sign shall be placed at a maximum height of 1900mm from the ground level. (3) Information expressed in a text format shall be supplemented with standard graphical symbols to facilitate comprehension. (4) Pedestrian signage shall be provided in relief and braille options. (5) Signages shall not be placed — (a) within close proximity ; and (b) in the case of visual material, too close to wall fixed signs. (6) In the case of a market, signage shall be erected at the entrance of a market and within the concourse of stalls to provide information and direction. (7) Audio-visual systems for information shall be installed on signages.

regs.title: Access to entertainment and recre- ational facilities.
regs.header: 29. Access to entertainment and recre- ational facilities.
regs.arrangement_title: Access to entertainment and recreational facilities
regs.text: 29. —(1) Accessible seating shall be provided for wheelchair users in accordance with Table 1.3 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Accessible seating shall be — (a) suitable to accommodate a person sitting beside a wheelchair user ; (b) provided in a range of vantage points within a building, where a seat is provided for non-disabled members of an audience. (3) A space adjacent to some seats shall be provided, to accomodate an assistance dog to rest away from the main circulation route. (4) Fire safety arrangements, including means of escape, shall comply with the relevant provisions prescribed under these Regulations.

regs.title: Sports fields and spectator areas.
regs.text: 30. —(1) Public sports fields, parking areas, entrances and spectator areas shall be accessible to persons with disabilities. (2) Controlled access points, including turnstiles, shall be designed to accommodate the free movement of mobility aids through an adjacent gate a minimum width of 915mm. (3) Level and accessible seating areas shall be provided beside sports fields for spectators and athletes with disabilities. (4) Public viewing areas shall be in accordance with the provisions on viewing areas, as specified under these Regulations. (5) Public toilets, urinals, bathrooms, and changing rooms shall be in accordance with provisions prescribed for outdoor amenities under these Regulations.

regs.title: Amphitheatres.
regs.text: 31. —(1) Exterior amphitheatres or performance arenas shall include seating areas made accessible to persons using mobility aids, with at least two spaces provided side by side, and a minimum of 3 percent of all spaces shall be reserved for persons using mobility aids. (2) Fixed or portable seating in an amphitheatre for persons using mobility aids shall be provided with back supports and armrests.

regs.title: Grandstands and viewing areas.
regs.text: 32. —(1) Where exterior grandstands and viewing areas are provided, accessible seating spaces for persons using mobility aids shall be made available in all price ranges, as specified Figures 1.036,1.037 and 1.039 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) A grandstand shall have — (a) a clear floor space of a minimum width of 900mm by depth of 1500mm, without reducing aisle space for side approach, and length of 1200mm for front or rear entry, as specified in Figure 1.036 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; and (b) accessible sitting areas for persons using mobility aids, with at least two spaces provided side by side, and a minimum of 3 percent of all spaces shall be reserved for persons using mobility aids. (3) Seating areas shall be level, and of firm and of non-slip material. (4) Where guardrails, handrails, or fences separate viewing areas from performance areas, care shall be taken to ensure that sightlines are appropriate. (5) Fixed or portable seating in an amphitheatre for persons using mobility aids shall be provided with back supports and armrests. (6) Seat heights shall be a maximum of 460mm and a minimum of 405mm, above floor level. (7) An aisle leading to accessible seating area shall have a slope of a maximum of 1:20 at any point, and the walkway behind wheelchair positions shall be a minimum width of 1200mm. (8) Viewing areas, including scenic lookouts, shall be accessible to persons using mobility aids. (9) Where a pay-per-view viewing lense is available, at least one location shall be accessible to persons using mobility aids, and viewing lense and controls shall be mounted at a maximum height of 1200mm above grade.

regs.title: Outdoor eating and entertainment spaces, balconies and terraces.
regs.header: 33. Outdoor eating and entertainment spaces, balconies and terraces.
regs.arrangement_title: Outdoor eating and entertainment spaces, balconies and terraces
regs.text: 33. —(1) Exterior residential, and public balconies or terraces shall be accessible from interior spaces with thresholds not exceeding a height of 13mm. (2) Where differences in elevation are unavoidable, short ramps with a maximum rise of 150mm, maximum pitch of 1 : 12, and a maximum length of 1200mm shall be utilized. (3) Balcony or terrace surfaces shall — (a) be of firm non-slip materials, and laid to slope gently at an angle of a minimum of 1 : 20 to ensure rapid removal of water ; (b) have a depth of a minimum of 1830mm to allow free rotation of mobility aids, as specified in Figure 1.040 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; (c) be designed to allow for clear vision below the rails for persons in a sitting position ; and (d) comply with Nigerian National Building Code requirements. (4) Doors opening out onto balconies or terraces shall be located where they open against a sidewall or rail.

regs.title: Boardwalks.
regs.text: 34. —(1) Where boardwalks are provided, including on a beach or waterfront locations, they shall be a minimum width of 1830mm to allow two wheelchairs pass with ease, as specified in Figure 1.041 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Boardwalk surface shall be of firm and non-slip materials, and where wooden boardwalks are provided, planks shall be laid normal to the expected path of travel, having a maximum joint width of 6mm. (3) Where the grade drop-off on a side exceeds 205mm, a contrasting and continuous stand-up edge of a minimum height of 1500mm shall be provided. (4) A handrail or other suitable guard may be provided, where a grade drop- off exceeds 460mm. (5) Roads, paths, sidewalks, or other pedestrian approaches to a boardwalk shall be accessible by a user of mobility aid through a level surface or ramped access point.

regs.title: Campgrounds.
regs.text: 35. —(1) 5 per cent of boarding facilities on a campground shall be located close to essential amenities, such as toilets and bathrooms. (2) A camp-ground shall be level with adjacent grades, be of a firm free draining surface, and have an obstruction free pathway. (3) Picnic tables and barbecue pits shall be close to campground, and easily accessible by a mobility aid user, as specified in See Figure 1.043 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) A camp-ground shall be equipped with — (a) accessible toilets and bathrooms or other campground amenities ; (b) an accessible charging point ; and (c) adjacent accessible parking, as specified in Figure 1.042 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Community mailboxes.
regs.text: 36. —(1) A community mailbox shall be located in conspicuous locations to a side of a pedestrian route or roadways. (2) Parking spaces or lay-bys at community mailboxes shall include sufficient space for a wheelchair user’s van. (3) An accessible kerb ramp shall be provided to allow access from the road surface or parking locations by various mobility aids, as specified in See Figure 1.044 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Community mailboxes shall be mounted on a level, firm, and free- draining surfaces, and have a minimum clear approach area of 1370mm by 1525mm. (5) Numbers on mailboxes shall be at a minimum height of 19mm, and of a colour or tone that is distinguishable from the mailbox surface. (6) Tactile markings and braille shall be provided at community mailboxes. (7) Waste cans shall be located close to community mailboxes and placed to one side of the expected paths of travel.

regs.title: Recreational Facilities.
regs.text: 37. —(1) Recreational facilities shall be accessible to persons with disabilities, as prescribed under these Regulations. (2) In the case of a gymnasium, exercise machines and equipment shall have a clear floor space to allow for easy access and navigation.

regs.title: Amusement rides.
regs.text: 38. —(1) Load or unload areas on an amusement rides shall have a ramp slope of a maximum of 1 : 8. (2) Accessible routes connecting an amusement ride in the load and unload area shall have a vertical difference between the floors of 16mm, and the horizontal gap of a maximum of 75mm (3) Wheelchair spaces shall be a minimum clear width of 760mm and a minimum clear length of 1220mm measured to a minimum height of 230mm above the floor surface. (4) Where wheelchair spaces are entered into from the side, an amusement ride shall have a minimum maneuvering clearance of 950mm x 1220mm. (5) Protrusion on an amusement ride shall be at a distance of — (a) 150mm along the front of the wheelchair space, where wheelchair space is measured at a minimum width of 230mm and maximum height of 685mm from the floor surface ; or (b) 635mm along the front of the wheelchair space, where wheelchair space is measured at a minimum of 685mm above the floor surface, as specified in Figure 2.068 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (6) A seat on an amusement ride shall- (a) be designed to allow for an independent transfer from a wheelchair ; (b) be located at a maximum height of 430mm to 485mm above the load and unload surface ; (c) be equipped with gripping surfaces and seat padding ; and (d) be free of sharp objects or obstruction in the path of transfer. (7) Where a series of transfer are required to reach a seat on an amusement ride the vertical transfer shall not exceed 205mm.

regs.title: Recreational Boating Facilities.
regs.text: 39. —(1) An accessible route serving a boat slip such as a gangway or series of gangways shall comply with the provisions of regulation 8 of these Regulations. (2) A boat slip may— (a) have a clear pier space measuring a minimum width of 1525mm wide ; and (b) for every maximum width of 3050mm linear pier edge serving the boat slip, contain a continuous clear opening of a minimum width of 1525mm wide. (3) Notwithstanding the provisions of sub-regulation (2) of this regulation, clear pier space for a boat slip may be permitted at a minimum width of 915mm for a length of 610mm maximum, provided that multiple 915mm wide segments shall be separated by elements that are 1525mm wide minimum and 1525mm long minimum. (4) Continuous clear openings on a boat slip shall have edge protection of a maximum height of 100mm and a maximum width of 51mm.

regs.title: Docks.
regs.text: 40. —(1) Fishing, boating, or swimming docks shall be accessible to persons with disabilities, as specified in Figures 1.045 and 1.046 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Paths, boardwalks and other routes to docks shall be made of level and firm material that provides direct access without elevation changes, and where sloppy road pavements are unavoidable, the gradient of the slope shall not be greater than 1 : 20, as specified in Figure 1.027 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) Grades steeper than 1 : 20 shall be designed as a ramp, with a slope gradient not greater than 1 : 12. (4) Handrails shall be provided on both sides of a ramp from 1 :20 gradient, as specified in Figure 1.027 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Sudden elevation changes of 205mm or less may be ramped at 1:8. (6) A guardrail shall be provided, where dock surfaces, such as floating ducks, are located more than 460mm above the water surface. (7) A contrasting stand-up edge of a minimum height of 150mm shall be provided on all exposed sides, where dock surfaces are 205mm or less above the water surface. (8) Steps and ramps shall provide a safe entering position as specified in Figure 1.053 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Swimming pools and wading pools.
regs.text: 41. —(1) Outdoor swimming and wading pools shall be easily accessible. (2) Swimming pools shall generally be of a "level-deck" designed to allow easy entry and exit from the pool. (3) A stand-up edge provided around a pool’s perimeter shall be a minimum height of 205mm and maximum height of 405mm, and the top edge shall have a width of 305mm to allow for a seated person. (4) Pool boundaries shall— (a) be clearly defined by a textural change ; (b) be of a bright colour or sharp contrast, to the water surface and the environment ; and (c) have surrounding paving, as specified in Figures 1.049 and 1.050 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Materials and finishes used on the pool perimeter, deck, or on paved areas surrounding the pool shall be of firm and non-slip materials. (6) Pool perimeter tiles or finishes shall be easy to clean and non-abrasive with chamfered edges at all pool boundary, to minimize the risk of injuries. (7) The wall and floor of a swimming pool shall have a light-coloured finish for increased safety. (8) Adequate floor drains that flush with the ground shall be provided on the pool deck to remove water quickly at all times. (9) Drainage tile, scuppers, or trenches shall be designed to minimize accidental tripping, and have no openings greater than 13mm in diameter. (10) Pool depth markings and signage shall be in highly contrasting colours and in large prints. (11) Where diving boards or platforms are provided, they shall be distinctively marked and protected to ensure that persons with visual disabilities do not accidentally walk below them. (12) Handrails shall be provided on both sides of access steps into the pool and extend a minimum length of 300mm onto the pool deck. (13) Swimming pool’s lanes or lane markers shall be in highly contrasting colours, and tie-off devices for lane markers shall be located where they do not constitute a potential tripping hazard. (14) Starter blocks for competitive racing shall be securely fixed in place. (15) Storage of safety gear or other equipment around the pool shall not be located where it constitutes a hazard. (16) Lifeguard chairs or other pool-related furniture shall be painted in highly contrasting colours. (17) Where there is no autonomous access into the pool, provision shall be made for transferring a person from a wheelchair into the pool, provided that where possible, permanent ramps shall be preferred to portable lifts. (18) A built-in ramp into a pool shall be sloped at a maximum of 1:12, with handrails on both sides and be positioned, where it does not interfere with swimming lanes, as specified in Figures 1.047 and 1.053 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Sloped entries to a swimming or wading pool.
regs.header: 42. Sloped entries to a swimming or wading pool.
regs.arrangement_title: Sloped entries to a swimming or wading pool
regs.text: 42. —(1) An alternative wheelchair made of corrosion resistant materials and specially designed for aquatic usage shall be provided to prevent pool contamination and prevent the damage to wheelchairs or other mobility aids. (2) Where sloped entries are provided, the surfaces of a pool shall be slip resistant. (3) A sloped entry of a swimming pool shall extend to a maximum depth of 760mm, below the stationary water level, and where landings are required, a minimum of one landing shall be located at the end of the slope, below the stationary water level. (4) Sloped entry and landings in a wading pool shall extend to the deepest part of the pool. (5) A slope entry into a pool shall — (a) have two handrails of a width of 1050mm on both sides of a sloped entry ; and (b) have on one side of the slope, a two-leveled handrail, with a clear width between handrails of 840mm minimum and 965mm maximum. (6) A clear deck space of a minimum of 1525mm by 1525mm with a slope not steeper than 1 : 48 shall be provided at the base of the transfer wall, provided that the clear deck space shall be centered on the — (a) grab bar, where one grab bar is provided ; or (b) clearance between the grab bars, where two grab bars are provided. (7) A transfer wall within the pool shall be— (a) at a distance of a minimum of 405mm and maximum of 485mm, measured from the deck ; (b) a minimum depth of 305mm and maximum of 405mm ; (c) a minimum length of 1525mm ; and (d) centered on the clear deck space. (8) Surfaces of transfer walls shall not be sharp and have rounded edges. (9) A minimum of one grab bar of 6.09mm width shall be provided on the transfer wall, and a grab bar shall be perpendicular to a pool wall and extends to full depth of the transfer wall. (10) The top of the gripping surface shall be a minimum of 100mm and maximum of 150mm above transfer walls. (11) Subject to sub-regulation (10) of this regulation, clearance space for a grab bar shall be a minimum of 610mm, as specified in Figure 1.052 and 1.053 to the First Schedule of these Regulations.

regs.title: Transfer platform in a pool.
regs.text: 43. —(1) A transfer platform shall be provided at the head of each transfer system, and be of a minimum depth of 485mm and minimum width of 610mm. (2) A transfer space of a minimum length and width of 1525mm with a slope not steeper than 1: 48 shall be provided at the base of a transfer platform surface, centered along a minimum of 610mm side of the transfer platform and the side of the transfer platform serving the transfer space shall be free from obstruction. (3) Transfer step height shall be a maximum of 205mm, and the surface of the bottom tread shall extend to a water depth of a minimum of 455mm below the stationary water level. (4) The surface of the transfer system shall not be sharp and shall have rounded edges. (5) A transfer step shall have a — (a) tread depth of a minimum of 355mm and a maximum of 430mm ; and (b) a tread width of a minimum of 610mm. (6) A minimum of one grab bar shall be provided on a transfer step or a continuous grab bar shall be provided on a flight of transfer steps. (7) The top of the gripping surface of a single or continuous grab bar shall be a minimum of 100mm and a maximum of 150mm above a transfer step and transfer platform. (8) The provisions of this regulation shall be as specified in Figures 1.055,1.056, 1.057, 1.058, 1.059 and 1.060 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Play grounds.
regs.text: 44. —(1) A playground shall have an accessible route from an accessible parking space with a clear width distance of a minimum of 1500mm, and a maximum slope of 1 :20. (2) The clear width of accessible routes connecting elevated play components shall be a minimum of 915mm. (3) Notwithstanding the provisions of sub-regulation (2) of this regulation, clear width of an accessible route connecting elevated play components may be reduced to a minimum of 815mm for a distance of a maximum of 610mm, provided the reduced width segment is separated by a segment that is of a minimum length of 1220mm and a minimum width of 915mm. (4) The clear width of transfer platform connecting elevated play components shall be permitted to be a minimum of 610mm. (5) A ramp shall be provided on a playground, — (a) where slope exceeds 1:20, (b) where the maximum slope for a ramp is 1:15, and (c) with a minimum width of 1015mm, between handrails, for a maximum sloped distance of 9000mm. (6) A landing shall — (a) have a minimum of 2 per cent cross-slope to allow adequate drainage, and accommodate changes of direction or rest sites ; and (b) comply with the provisions on ramps in these Regulations. (7) The surface of a route on a playground shall be firm, slip-resistant, and capable of easy draining. (8) For ease of supervision, play areas shall be separated according to age category by age-appropriate equipment, facilities, or other amenities. (9) Play components shall be linked to an accessible route through the playground. (10) A play component shall be situated in a designated location and free from obstruction. (11) A play component which has a seat or entry point shall make provision for an unobstructed transfer from a mobility aid. (12) A play table shall provide knee clearance with a minimum height of 610mm, minimum depth of 430mm, and minimum width of 760mm, and the tops of rims, curbs or other obstructions shall be of a maximum height of 785mm, as set out in Figures 1.063 and1.064 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (13) Amenities located on a playground such as public toilets and bathrooms, changing rooms, and telephones shall be accessible to persons with disabilities in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations. (14) Resting furniture such as benches shall be located near paths and walkways. (15) Grades in accessible picnic areas shall not be greater than 1 :30. (16) Some accessible parking spaces shall be located within 30000mm to accessible picnic areas.

regs.title: Terraces and patios of a public building.
regs.header: 45. Terraces and patios of a public building.
regs.arrangement_title: Terraces and patios of a public building
regs.text: 45. —(1) Access from outdoor areas into interior areas shall be leveled, or have a sloped threshold not exceeding 13mm. (2) Where there is grade difference of — (a) 150mm or less, a short ramp of 1:20 shall be created ; or (b) more than 150mm exists, a ramp of 1:15 shall be created. (3) Terrace and patios shall be of firm and level materials laid to drain at slopes of not more than 1 : 50, and joints in patio or terrace materials shall be a maximum width of 6mm. (4) A patio or terrace that is 600mm or more above grade shall have suitable guards, and the top rail of such guards or handrails shall allow a seated person to clearly see below the rail. (5) Where a patio or terrace is 205mm to 460mm above grade, a cane detectable stand-up edge of a minimum height of 150mm, shall be provided. (6) Where several patios or terraces are provided, wind and sun protection shall be required, for persons with disabilities who prefer to sit in a protected location.

regs.title: Path and footbridges.
regs.text: 46. —(1) A path, and footbridge shall be as specified in Figure 1.066 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Where a path or footbridge has a slope exceeding 1 : 20, an alternate route which consist of steps and ramps shall be provided nearby. (3) Where steps, ramps, or footbridges are required, the - (a) bridge surface shall be made of non-slip materials ; and (b) bridge shall have handrails and guards, as specified in Figure 1.068 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) A slope on a bridge shall not exceed 1 : 20.

regs.title: Open Viewing location and instrument.
regs.text: 47. —(1) A viewing location, for viewing landmarks, special features, wildlife, entertainment and sports activities shall be accessible to a mobility aid user. (2) A viewing instrument, such as telescope shall be lowered at a height of 1000mm for persons with disabilities.

regs.title: Waterfront areas.
regs.text: 48. —(1) Waterfront areas in a park or other recreation facilities open to the public shall be designed to accommodate persons with disabilities. (2) Provision for accessible parking area, entrance, path, and seating arrangement in a waterfront area shall conform with the provisions of these Regulations.

regs.title: Wildlife reserves and conservation areas.
regs.text: 49. —(1) Wildlife reserves and conservation areas open to the public shall have accessible parking areas, entrances, paths, trails, and footbridges in line with the provisions of these Regulations. (2) Rest areas shall be located near an accessible route and be equipped with the appropriate furniture, as specified in Figure 1.069 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) Clear sign post and other relevant indicators shall be provided to point out special lookout locations or wildlife viewing areas. (4) A tactile map, including map with a raised outline, of paths and other features in a wildlife reserve or conservation area shall be provided at the start of the path and placed strategically along the path, as specified in Figure 1.070 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Market places.
regs.text: 50. Persons with disabilities shall have access to a market place.

regs.title: Walkways and aisles.
regs.text: 51. A walkway or aisle between stalls or edges of vending tables shall be of a minimum width of 3000mm.

regs.title: Vending tables.
regs.text: 52. A vending table or counter in a stall shall measure a maximum height of 1000mm and shall not protrude or obstruct the main pedestrian traffic flow.

regs.title: Fire safety.
regs.text: 53. —(1) Provisions for fire prevention, protection and safety arrangements including means of escape shall be in accordance with fire safety standards issued by relevant authority. (2) Access routes shall be created for fire tenders to access stalls and shall meet fire safety standards issued by relevant authority.

regs.title: Access to seating area.
regs.text: 54. —(1) Access to seating in public waiting areas shall be direct and unobstructed and easily identifiable by persons with disabilities. (2) Clear space for access to a seating area shall be of a minimum - (a) width of 900mm in front of a row of seats or 1200mm where practicable, to allow access by persons with mobility aids along a cross-aisle as specified in Figure 1.071 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; and (b) width of 1050mm and minimum depth of 2300mm to allow for maneuvering a wheelchair into a designated space from a circulation route at right angles, as specified in Figure 1.072 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) A seating area shall be equipped with seats, and the seat height or the compressed cushion height for fixed seating, shall be between 450mm and 475mm.

regs.title: Access to outdoor amenities.
regs.text: 55. Outdoor amenities, facilities, or equipment shall be available to persons with disabilities.

regs.title: Benches and seats.
regs.text: 56. —(1) Exterior benches or seats shall be located to a side of a public walkway or path, and be mounted on a leveled firm base, such as a concrete pad or brick pavers, as specified in Figure 1.083 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) A fixed bench shall measure at a height between 405mm and 460mm, as specified in Figure 1.083 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) A clearance area or space measuring 1015mm by 1220mm shall be available beside a bench. (4) A bench shall have seats measuring a minimum length of 1065mm, minimum width of 510mm and a maximum depth of 610mm. (5) Where practicable, a grab bar may be provided on a wall adjacent to a bench or seat to provide assisted transfer to bench, but not on the seat back, provided that the grab bar shall not obstruct transfer to a bench or seat. (6) The surface of a bench or seat shall be slip-resistant and not accumulate water. (7) The provision of this regulation shall be as specified in Figure 1.073 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Bicycle and motorcycle racks.
regs.text: 57. Bicycle and motorcycle racks shall be located to a side of a sidewalk, path, or entrance, and not constitute an obstruction.

regs.title: Drinking fountains.
regs.text: 58. —(1) A public drinking fountain shall be securely mounted on a firm base, and have a clear knee space of a minimum width of 700mm, as specified in Figure 1.074 and 1.075 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Where a drinking fountain is recessed or fitted, such as in an alcove, the— (a) knee space below the fountain shall measure a minimum width of 760mm ; (b) spout shall measure a maximum height of 915mm ; and (c) controls shall be easily operable with one hand.

regs.title: Accessible restrooms.
regs.text: 59. —(1) An accessible restroom shall be integrated within public toilet facilities, and separately accessible by men and women. . (2) An accessible restroom shall be provided on each floor in a multi-storey building. (3) An accessible restroom shall be— (a) reached through an accessible circulation paths with clear directional signs ; and (b) clearly labeled with the internationally recognised symbol of accessibility, together with written and tactile informative descriptions. (4) An accessible restroom shall have a sliding door or a door that opens outwards to allow more space for a wheelchair to be maneuvered inside. (5) The door referred to in sub-regulation (4) of this regulation shall have the capacity to be locked from the inside, and released on the outside in case of emergency. (6) An accessible restroom shall — (a) have a clear turning space measuring 1500mm by 1500mm to ensure easy navigation without obstruction ; (b) be well-drained, and have waterproof, non-slippery and non-glare floor surface ; (c) have sufficient natural and artificial light, good ventilation, and be free from loud background noise, strong smell, and flickering lights ; and (d) have pull alarm system mounted on the ceiling near a toilet and suspended at a height of 1100mm from the floor. (7) The colour of critical elements or facilities in an accessible restroom shall contrast with the background. (8) A fire alarm shall be installed in the accessible toilet with visual and audible signals.

regs.title: Toilet.
regs.text: 60. —(1) A toilet shall — (a) be positioned in the corner of the room, and the centre line of the toilet shall be positioned at a maximum of 500mm from the sidewall ; and (b) have a clear space measuring a minimum of 900mm on the open side of the toilet. (2) A toilet seat shall measure at a maximum height of 480mm. (3) The following equipment shall be easy to operate and shall be positioned near a toilet, at a maximum height of 1100mm above the floor— (a) toilet paper dispenser ; (b) flush control, where it is hand-operated ; and (c) detachable bidet shower head. (4) A sanitary bin shall be located near the toilet. (5) A toilet shall have a — (a) a moveable U-grab bar on the open side of the toilet ; and (b) grab bar measuring a length of 600mm on the sidewall, located not more than 250mm from the rear wall and at a maximum height of 680mm. (6) The provision of this regulation shall be as specified in Figure 1.077 and 1.078 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Washbasins.
regs.text: 61. —(1) A washbasin, soap, paper towel dispenser and hand sanitiser shall be provided near a toilet, at a maximum height of 1100mm from the floor. (2) The rim of the washbasin shall measure a maximum of 740mm from the floor. (3) A washbasin shall have a knee space underneath the washbasin. (4) A tap shall be installed on a side of the washbasin and operable one- handed, with lever action and not twist action. (5) A vertical grab bar shall be mounted around a washbasin. (6) A mirror may be fitted above the washbasin, with the lower edge measuring a maximum height of 600mm from the floor.

regs.title: Accessible washrooms.
regs.text: 62. —(1) In a public building, a minimum of one washroom equipped with accessibility features shall be reserved for persons with disabilities, as a stand- alone bathroom or incorporated within an accessible restroom. (2) An accessible washroom shall be clearly labeled with the internationally recognised symbol of accessibility and relevant written informative description, and accessed through a clearly marked accessible path. (3) An accessible washroom shall have a sliding door or a door that opens outwards to allow more space for a wheelchair to be maneuvered inside. (4) The door referred to in sub-regulation (3) of this regulation shall have the capacity to be locked from the inside, and released on the outside in case of emergency. (5) An accessible washroom shall — (a) measure a minimum of 2000mm by 2200mm in size, with a clear turning space of 1500mm by 1500mm ; (b) be well-drained, and have a waterproof, non-slippery and non-glare floor surface ; (c) have natural and artificial light, good ventilation ; and (d) be free from loud background noise, strong smells, and flickering lights. (6) Lighting levels in a washroom shall be evenly distributed and no less than 100lux. (7) A washroom and its compartments shall be as specified in and Figure 2.073 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Shower compartment.
regs.text: 63. —(1) A shower compartment shall — (a) measure a minimum of 1200mm by 1200mm ; (b) be fitted with a foldable seat measuring a maximum height of 480mm, with a backrest, and the centre line of the seat shall be positioned a maximum of 500mm from the sidewall ; (c) be fitted with a curtain, which can be drawn while in a sitting position ; and (d) be fitted with a pull alarm system mounted on the ceiling, and suspended at a height of 100mm from the floor. (2) A folding grab bar shall be fixed — (a) on the open side of a bath or shower seat, at a distance of 820mm from the sidewall, and at a maximum height of 680mm ; (b) in front of a bath or shower seat at a distance of 900mm from the rear wall ; and (c) on the wall on the side of a bath or shower seat. (3) Where a washroom is fitted with a shower — (a) a shower head shall be positioned at a — (i) distance of 500mm from the rear wall, in the case of a fixed shower, or (ii) maximum height of 1100mm and at a distance of 500mm from the rear wall, in the case of a detachable shower head ; and (b) shower controls shall be located on the wall beside a shower seat, at a maximum height of 1000mm and distance of 500mm from the rear wall. (4) Shower controls shall be easy to operate one-handed, with lever action and not twist action. (5) The emergency alarm system shall be positioned inside the shower compartment, and be reachable and operable (6) An easy to reach shelf and towel rail shall be positioned outside the shower compartment.

regs.title: Bath compartment.
regs.text: 64. —(1) A bath compartment shall — (a) measure a minimum length of 2440mm and minimum width of 1955mm ; (b) be fitted with a bath tub, equipped with the following— (i) a transfer seat measuring a minimum depth of 380mm, level with the bath rim and located at the end of a bath tub opposite the bath controls, and (ii) a 915mm horizontal grab-rail, mounted at a height of 835mm on the long sidewall. (2) The bath rim shall measure at a maximum height of 480mm from the floor level. (3) Faucets and controls shall be of the "single-lever action" handle type.

regs.title: Public telephones.
regs.text: 65. —(1) Where public telephones are provided in exterior settings, a minimum of one telephone shall be designed to be wheelchair accessible. (2) A telephone shall be positioned on a side of a path of travel or walkway, clear of obstacles, and have clear space for access by persons using mobility aids. (3) A telephone provided pursuant to these Regulations shall be — (a) equipped to accommodate persons with disabilities, including persons with hearing disabilities ; (b) equipped with teletypewriter telephone devices (TTY devices) ; and (c) clearly marked with an internationally recognized symbol for persons with disabilities, as specified in Figure 1.076 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Where a telephone enclosure or recess is required the enclosure or recess shall measure a width of 760mm with knee space below the phone shelf or equipment measuring a minimum of 685mm clear. (5) Telephone controls and slots shall be mounted at a maximum height of 1200mm, as specified in Figure 1.086 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Zebra crossing and pedestrian signals.
regs.text: 66. —(1) Signals at pedestrian crosswalks shall — (a) be designed in accordance with the requirements of the Nigeria Highway Code ; (b) have a clearly marked pedestrian button to be mounted on a pole beside a curb cut, at a maximum height of 1065mm ; and (c) be equipped with tactile features on pushbuttons, and audible and flashing crossing signals shall be provided, as an aid to persons who have hearing or visual disabilities. (2) Visual display screen shall be visible enough to be seen, and audible pedestrian signals shall be loud and heard clearly above ambient noise at a minimum of 15 decibels louder than the ambient noise. (3) The Commission, in collaboration with the appropriate authority, shall issue guidelines on the configuration of audible pedestrian signals, in line with international standards.

regs.title: Lighting for exterior areas not including roads.
regs.header: 67. Lighting for exterior areas not including roads.
regs.arrangement_title: Lighting for exterior areas not including roads
regs.text: 67. —(1) Exterior lighting on public thoroughfares and along pedestrian routes shall be designed in accordance with Nigerian Highway Code , as specified in Figures 1.080 and 1.081 of the First Schedule to these Regulations, and the lighting levels shall be a minimum of 30lux. (2) Lighting sources shall be selected and located at, or beside steps and stairs to ensure clear definition of treads, risers, and nosing. (3) Supplementary lighting shall be provided to highlight key way-finding signage. (4) Lighting standard or post shall be mounted to a side of a path or walkway, and not constitute a hazard. (5) An overhead light fixture shall be mounted on a standard with a clear headroom measuring height of 2030mm. (6) Lighting of landscape on special site features shall be designed and installed to minimize direct glare, as specified in Figure 1.081 of the First Schedule of these Regulations. (7) The Commission, in collaboration with the relevant authorities, may issue guidelines specifying lighting levels, colour spectrum, and other characteristics for light on public thoroughfares.

regs.title: Public address systems.
regs.text: 68. —(1) Public address systems provided outdoors or at an exterior recreation or entertainment facilities shall be free from sound distortion, and provide a full spectrum of sound. (2) Loudspeakers of an address system shall be located to cover the desired area adequately without feedback noise, and be mounted on posts to ensure that the output close to speakers is at acceptable acoustic levels for targeted audience. (3) Where information is to be announced, a clear warning comprising both visual and audio signals shall be provided before the announcement. (4) Where practicable, a Frequency Modulation (FM) loop or other suitable systems for persons with hearing disabilities may be provided where large outdoor concerts are regularly performed, as specified in Figure 1.082 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Way-finding.
regs.text: 69. Clear directional instructions that are easily perceived and understood with little or no assistance by persons with disabilities shall be provided.

regs.title: Traffic signals.
regs.text: 70. —(1) Traffic light timing at specific sites shall be adjustable to — (a) suit the volume of vehicular and pedestrian traffic ; (b) suit walking speed of pedestrians, particularly of persons with disabilities ; and (c) provide audible and visual cues, as specified in Figure 1.079 and 1.083 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) A traffic signal shall - (a) indicate when it is safe to walk or drive ; (b) operate consistently with visible pedestrian signals ; (c) in the case of an audible traffic signal, be capable of being heard above the ambient traffic noise levels ; and (d) differentiate directional crossings. (3) A pedestrian crossings signal shall be — (a) capable of being activated by pedestrians waiting to cross ; and (b) equipped with tactile features on a pushbutton , to aid persons who have both hearing and visual disabilities. (4) A traffic light shall be mounted on a level surface that is identified with textured paving, and have buttons for pedestrian initiated calls. (5) The button referred to in sub-regulation (4) of this regulations shall be— (a) mounted at a height of 1065mm ; (b) easily identifiable by colour and profile ; and (c) equipped with a locator tone. (6) Obstacles and free standing objects shall not be located on the level approach area or within 990mm of the normal pedestrian approach to the call button location, as specified in Figure 1.084 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Visual and tactile cues.
regs.text: 71. Visual and tactile cues shall be included in the design of the built environment for safe navigation.

regs.title: Colour, pattern and texture.
regs.text: 72. —(1) Colour intensity and contrast with adjacent colours shall be utilized to — (a) define boundaries of objects or to distinguish lettering from their background colour ; and (b) provide information. (2) Signage shall be designed using highly visible and contrasting colours, as specified in Figure 1.085 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) Colour or Tone contrast of approximately 70 per cent light reflectance shall be provided on signage, and finishes on signage shall be matte to minimize glare. (4) Textured surfaces shall be used to indicate potential hazards, such as, level changes at ramps and stairs. (5) For the purpose of a textured paving strip, a one pace depth of 915mm shall be provided at the head of stairs or ramps, or where a walking hazard may exist, as specified in Figure 1.086 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (6) Textured surfaces used as warning devices shall be cane-detectable, and clearly differentiated from surrounding paving surfaces, as specified in Figure 1.087 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (7) Textured surfaces such as saw-cut concrete, with regular grooves shall be positioned at a maximum distance of 50mm apart, with the grooves being perpendicular to the path of travel.

regs.title: Construction site.
regs.text: 73. —(1) A construction site shall have a boundary protection to minimize hazard and provide easy access, as specified in Figure 1.086 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) A construction hoarding shall be firmly constructed with supports and bracing, which permits free movement by pedestrians, particularly persons using various mobility aids. (3) Overhead framing or bracing shall ensure clear headroom of a minimum of 2030mm above the sidewalk. (4) Cane detectable temporary barriers shall be provided around short-term repair sites, such as sidewalk repairs, manhole access cover, and etc., as an aid to persons with visual disabilities, as specified in Figure 1.087 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Where at a construction site or maintenance location, a clear pedestrian route of 1100mm is not achievable through the normal route, an alternative safe and level pedestrian routes shall be provided with suitable protection from vehicular traffic. (6) Where hoardings with public viewing ports are provided, a minimum of one viewing port shall be mounted at a point not exceeding 1220mm on centre, for use by persons using mobility aids.

regs.title: Freestanding objects.
regs.text: 74. —(1) Freestanding objects shall be located to a side of a pedestrian route, path, or walkway, designated amenity strips, or recesses without limiting the width of the route or constituting a hazard, as specified in Figures 1.088 and 1.089 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Free standing objects include— (a) permanent objects such as bollards, bicycle racks, benches, bus shelters, newspaper vending boxes, mailboxes, hydrants, light standards, trees, etc. ; and (b) temporary objects such as queuing lines, sales booths, loose garbage receptacles, guy wires, etc. (3) Objects with height between 685mm and 2030mm above the finished floor or ground shall not protrude beyond a length of 100mm into a circulation path, as specified in Figure 1.090 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Waste handling infrastructure.
regs.text: 75. —(1) A waste receptacle shall be — (a) mounted in a designated location, and to a side of a pedestrian route, path, or walkway, so as not to constitute a hazard ; and (b) accessible to persons using mobility aids, except for large industrial containers. (2) A waste receptacle, container, or box, including recycling box, shall be large enough to contain the anticipated quantity of waste in a location. (3) A waste receptacle in a landscaped area, recreation, and picnic area shall be conspicuous and clearly identified by suitable colours or signage. (4) The paving around waste receptacles shall be level, firm, free draining. and easy to wash down. (5) Where a covered waste receptacle is being used, the waste receptacle cover shall be easy to lift with one hand. (6) Temporary construction scows or large mobile industrial containers shall be located away from normal pedestrian routes. (7) Where a wall-mounted or recessed waste receptacle is being used, bin liners shall be easy to remove from the waste receptacle. (8) Vehicular access routes to garbage containers for maintenance purposes shall not cross pedestrian routes.

regs.title: Gates and openings.
regs.text: 76. —(1) Where a gate or opening is provided through a fence or screen to a public use area, such opening shall be accessible, and measure a minimum width of 915mm. (2) Gate hardware shall be suitable for autonomous use, and closing devices shall not be spring-loaded. (3) Where a turnstile or other ticketing device is not accessible, an accessible nearby gate or opening shall be provided. (4) Gate openings shall be measured at minimum width of 815mm. (5) Maneuvering clearances shall extend the entire width of a doorway and latch side or hinge side clearance, as specified in Tables 2.5 and 2.6. of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Landscape materials and planting.
regs.text: 77. —(1) Plants with thorns and heavy berries shall not be located on or along the path of an active pedestrian route. (2) Planter beds shall measure a maximum height of 460mm above grade, and planting bed edges adjacent to a busy pedestrian route shall measure a minimum height of 100mm. (3) Overhanging branches of trees or shrubs, located over walkways or paths, shall be trimmed to ensure that the headroom over the walking space measures a minimum height of 2030mm, and pedestrian routes, paths, or walkways shall be clear of branches, thorns, and other obstructions at all times. (4) An easement shall be provided at 20000mm from restricted areas.

regs.title: Materials and finishes.
regs.text: 78. —(1) Paving surfaces for walkways and pedestrian routes shall be constructed using materials such as bitumen surface, concrete, interlocking bricks, or patio stones, provided that the joints connecting the paving surfaces do not exceed a width of 6mm, and the level variations do not exceed a height of 6mm in height. (2) All paving shall be laid to drain easily. (3) Gratings or grills shall be located on a side of a pedestrian route or walkway ; provided that, where it is impracticable to have gratings or grills on a side of the pedestrian walkway, gratings or grills shall be located at right angles to the normal path of travel, with openings measuring a maximum width of 13mm, as specified in Figures 1.095 and 1.096, of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Steps shall be of non-slip materials with highly contrasted nosings. (5) Ramp surfaces shall be firm and of non-slip materials, and laid perpendicular to the path of travel. (6) Handrails and guardrails shall be continuous, smooth and well maintained. (7) Walls adjacent to ramps or stairs shall be in non-abrasive finishes.

regs.title: Maintenance of outdoor features.
regs.text: 79. —(1) Pedestrian routes shall be well maintained to permit safe circulation of pedestrian movement. (2) A pedestrian route or walkway leading to an accessible entrance and exit shall be kept free of obstacles. (3) Garbage containers shall be emptied regularly to avoid the accumulation of extraneous materials around the containers. (4) Light bulbs along pedestrian routes shall be replaced on a regular schedule, along with lamp having the same wattage. (5) Gates, closers, automatic door operators, porch lifts, automatic ticket machines or other essential equipment shall be inspected and well maintained on a regular schedule.

regs.title: Safety and security.
regs.text: 80. —(1) Lighting shall be provided over thoroughfares, steps and ramps, as specified in Figure 1.097 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Pedestrian routes shall be designed to provide clear lines of sight to ensure personal safety wherever possible. (3) The Commission shall, in collaboration with the relevant authorities, make guidelines for the provision of communication devices, alert systems, muster plan, and other emergency evacuation strategies.

regs.title: Pathway from a parking space to the building.
regs.header: 81. Pathway from a parking space to the building.
regs.arrangement_title: Pathway from a parking space to the building
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 81. —(1) A pathway from a parking space to a building shall measure a minimum head height of 2100mm and a minimum width of 1200mm between a parking bay and a building (2) Pathway surfaces shall be flat, firm, made of non-slippery materials, and kept clear of hazards and other obstacles at both ground level and higher level.
