(3) An accessible ramp access point shall be provided, where there is a kerb along a pathway. (4) Tactile paving strips shall be — (a) used on public routes to assist persons with visual disabilities ; and (b) of contrasting colours with the rest of the pavement.

regs.title: Canopies and weather protection.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 82. —(1) A main entrance and critical pathway connecting different parts of a facility shall be protected by a suitable canopy or overhang. (2) A canopy projecting over a passenger boarding zone shall, provide a headroom clearance measuring a minimum of 3555mm to accommodate a special transit vehicle or other vehicle conveying persons with disabilities, as specified in Figure 1.098 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) Where a balcony is provided as part of a build environment, it shall be equipped to protect against wind, rain and sun.

regs.title: Entrance.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 83. —(1) Mobility aids shall be available on request at public buildings, and be positioned carefully so as not to constitute an obstruction. (2) A tactile pictographic map of a building shall be installed near its entrance to provide a visual guide or information on the structure and parts of the building. (3) Interior routes to accessible entrances and accessible exits shall be safe and easy to navigate by persons with disabilities. (4) An entrance door shall — (a) contrast visually with its immediate surroundings, (b) be well lit and clearly signed ; and (c) not have a mirrored finish. (5) An accessible entrance shall — (a) provide basic protection from the weather, and include doors and vestibules that are independently operated by persons with disabilities ; (b) be fitted with security locks ; and (c) be equipped with a communication device.

regs.title: Reception area or information desk.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 84. —(1) A reception area or information desk shall be located at a building entrance for easy identification, and access to the edge of a counter or reception desk shall be direct and unobstructed. (2) Where a building provides a reception area or information desk, the area or desk shall be — (a) clearly marked and identifiable from the entrance ; (b) approached through an accessible path ; and (c) designed to ensure the easy access of a wheelchair user and person with dwarfism. (3) Where a reception area or information desk is fitted with a counter, a section of the counter shall— (a) be lowered to a maximum height of 760mm and have a minimum width of 1500mm ; (b) have a knee space measuring a height of 700mm from the floor and a depth of 500mm from the base of the counter ; and (c) have a minimum work surface depth measuring 700mm. (4) The front of the counter referred to in sub-regulation (3) of this regulation shall have a clear maneuvering space measuring a minimum depth of 1200mm and width of 1800mm, as specified in Figure 2.032 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) The accessible section of the counter shall be clearly marked with an internationally recognized symbol of accessibility. (6) A reception area or information desk may, where practicable, provide— (a) a hearing loop, and the hearing loop shall be clearly marked ; (b) materials in accessible formats for persons with disabilities ; and (c) sign language interpretation services. (7) A knee recess to accommodate the feet of a wheelchair user and the footplate of a wheelchair shall be provided. (8) Where queuing is the normal pattern of use, permanent or temporary control barriers shall be designed to allow for wheelchairs to— (a) turn towards the counter or desk ; (b) pass behind a person already in position at another window or desk ; or (c) turn around and leave. (9) Where the floor surface on the receptionist’s side of a counter is on a higher level than on the visitor’s side, a ramp with a gradient not greater than 1:20 or steeper, shall be provided to allow easy access.

regs.title: Doors and doorways.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 85. —(1) A main entrance door, and other accessible entrance and exit door shall measure a minimum width of 915mm to allow easy access of persons using mobility aids. (2) Where an automatic door is in use, the door shall be defined by a highly contrasting colours and textured surface at grade. (3) An entrance fitted with a door or any form of barricade shall be fitted with a guard measuring a minimum clearance of 305mm between the guard and the opened door or barricade, as specified in Figure 2.003 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Where a building is finished with glazing materials, door frames shall be clearly colour-differentiated to aid in locating the entrance, as specified in Figure 2.004 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) The Commission, in collaboration with relevant agencies, may develop guidelines specifying the sizes and other specifications for doors and entrances.

regs.title: Self-closing swing doors.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 86. —(1) The minimum clear width of a single leafed door, or one leaf or the primary leaf of a double-leafed door, clear of any projections from the face of the door, shall be as shown in Table 2.4 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Subject to sub-regulation (1) of this regulation, the method of measuring clear width shall be as specified in Figures 2.003 and 2.004 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Power- operated or automated doors.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 87. —(1) A low energy power-operated or automated door shall be used as a swing door, and safety provisions for the low energy power-operated door shall conform to requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering. (2) Where a building is fitted with revolving doors, a complementary accessible door, which is — (a) low energy-operated or automated, or manual door ; and (b) properly marked, shall be provided immediately adjacent to the revolving door, and available for use at all times.

regs.title: Double-leaf doors and gates.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 88. Where a building is fitted with a double leafed door or gate, one of active leaves or primary leaf of the doors or gates shall comply with following— (a) a door opening — (i) shall measure a minimum clear width of 815mm, (ii) in the case of swinging doors, shall be 90 degrees between the face of the door, when opened, and the stop, and (iii) above a depth of 610mm shall have a minimum clear opening of 915mm ; (b) no projection shall be permitted into a clear opening width lower than 865mm above the finish floor or ground, provided that where there is clear width of doors measured between 865mm and 2030mm, allowable projection shall not exceed 100mm above the finish floor or ground ; (c) projection shall not exceed a maximum length of 16mm for the latch side stop ; (d) a door closer and door stop shall measure at a minimum height of 1980mm above the finish floor or ground ; (e) a minimum maneuvering clearance at a door or gate, which extends the full width of the doorway, and require latch side or hinge side clearance, shall comply with Table 2.1of the First Schedule of these Regulations ; and (f ) in the case of a hospital patient room, an entry door shall not be required to provide clearance beyond the latch side of the door.

regs.title: Doorways without doors.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 89. A doorway without a door or gate measuring less than 915mm shall have a manoeuvring clearance, and comply with Table 2.2. of the First Schedule of these Regulations.

regs.title: Recessed doors or gates.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 90. Maneuvering clearance for forwarding approach shall be— (a) provided where an obstruction within 455mm of the latch side of a doorway projects more than 205mm beyond the face of the door ; (b) measured perpendicular to the face of the door or gate ; and (c) of equal floor level or ground surface, and changes in level shall not be permitted.

regs.title: Door and gate hardware, locks and closers.
regs.header: 91. Door and gate hardware, locks and closers.
regs.arrangement_title: Door and gate hardware, locks and closers
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 91. —(1) Where practicable, an automatic door opener may be provided. (2) A pushbutton or card access control used to control a door or gate shall be— (a) located away from the door swing ; (b) mounted on a wall or post, at a height between 1000mm and 1100mm measured to the centre of the control from the ground level ; (c) distinct in colour or texture on one side ; and (d) brailed and have raised numbers or letters. (3) A pushbutton shall measure 150mm in diameter. (4) Doors in a series such as in a vestibule, shall measure a minimum of 2135mm apart, and the clear opening between door swings shall not be less than 1200mm. (5) Door hardware, including pulls and push plates, shall be mounted between 915mm and 1065mm from grade. (6) A door opening hardware in an entrance, vestibule, and room doors shall be easy to grasp and use, as specified in Figure 2.010 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (7) Hardware for closet doors, drawer pulls, and holders shall be of Simple ‘D’ type, with a range length of 75mm to 100mm, as specified in Figure 2.011 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (8) A door lock shall be mounted between the height of 760mm and 1065mm from ground level. (9) A sliding door operating hardware shall — (a) be exposed and usable from both sides ; (b) be easy to grasp and use ; and (c) not reduce the effective clear opening width below 810mm, as specified in Figures, 2.009 and 1.071 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (10) Where out-swinging doors are being used, an additional pull handle shall be mounted horizontally, and close to the hinge side of the door.

regs.title: Manual door opening and closing devices.
regs.header: 92. Manual door opening and closing devices.
regs.arrangement_title: Manual door opening and closing devices
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 92. —(1) Door opening furniture shall be designed to be operated one- handed, with lever action and not twist action. (2) Security and fire exit fittings, such as short lever turn buttons, bolts, latches or locks, shall be easy to handle or operate. (3) Torque force required to operate a key and cylinder turn shall not exceed 0.5 Nm. (4) For easy identification by persons with visual disabilities — (a) a door hardware shall contrast visually with the surface of a door ; and (b) a pull handle shall not be fitted on the push side of a door. (5) The location and design of a lever and pull handles for both external and internal doors shall be as set out in Figures 2.011, 2.012, and 2.013 of the First Schedule to these Regulations, and be maintained consistently throughout a building. (6) Where a lever intercepts a viewing panel, a projecting glazing bead shall not interfere with the operation of the lever or reduce the effective clearance behind it.

regs.title: Controlled doors opening and closing devices.
regs.header: 93. Controlled doors opening and closing devices.
regs.arrangement_title: Controlled door opening and closing devices
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 93. —(1) For the purposes of access through a single or double swing door, the opening force of a door, when measured at the leading edge of the door, shall not exceed — (a) 30 N from 0° of the door in the closed position to 30° open ; and (b) 22.5 N from 30° to 60° of the opening cycle. (2) A controlled door closing device, with or without a back check, shall allow the door to open sufficiently to provide the required effective clear width. (3) The maximum closing force exerted by a controlled door closing device shall be within 0° and 15° of final closure.

regs.title: Hinges.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 94. —(1) A single-axis hinge and the fixing positions of a hinge shall conform to the requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering. (2) Where it is necessary to minimize resistance to door opening and closing, hinges with low friction bearings shall be used to carry the appropriate mass of the door.

regs.title: Locks and latches.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 95. —(1) Locks, cylinders, and latches shall conform to the requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering. (2) Where an upright mortise lock or latch is used, cylinder shall be placed above or below the lever handle, to ensure an unobstructed access to the keyway. (3) Where, subject to sub regulation (2) of this regulation, a cylinder is placed below the handle, the minimum distance between the lever handle and the keyway of the locking mechanism shall be 72mm. (4) The height of the lever handle shall be as specified in Figure 2.012 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Where a multi-point locking system is used, it shall be capable of being locked and unlocked by a single turn of the key, and the operating height of a lever or pad handle shall be as specified in Figure 2.013 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (6) The Commission, in collaboration with the relevant authorities, may make guidelines specifying suitable locks cylinders and latches for use in buildings.

regs.title: Door bolts
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 96. —(1) A door required to be bolted for security purposes shall have a at least one of the following bolts— (a) knob slide flush bolts or surface bolts with a free moving slide action ; (b) rack and pinion mortise bolts fitted with fixed knobs to enable the user to operate them easily without the need for inserting a loose key into a restricted hole ; (c) surface-mounted or mortised espagnolette bolt with top and bottom shoots or side shoots, operated by a single handle positioned at a height between 900mm and 1050mm, from the finished floor level ; or (d) lever-action flush bolts, provided that countersunk slide bolts, which are both flush and surface-mounted, shall not be used. (2) A door bolt shall conform to the requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering. (3) Release forces for panic exit devices operated by a horizontal bar for use on escape routes shall conform to the requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering. (4) Release forces for emergency exit devices operated by a “Type A” lever handle and a “Type B” push pad shall conform to the requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering.

regs.title: Glazed screens and sidelights.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 97. —(1) Fully glazed sidelights at exterior entrances or in interior vestibules, and fully glazed screens used within a building, shall be clearly identifiable so as not to constitute a hazard for persons with visual disabilities. (2) A row of bright decals or a continuous opaque stripe, measuring a minimum width of 50mm and of highly contrasting colour shall be mounted at eye level, between 1350mm and 1500mm from the finished floor. (3) A decal shall— (a) be located at a maximum of 150mm on centre ; (b) be a minimum width of 50mm ; and (c) with respect to the solid portion of the design or logo, be bold for easy identification by persons with visual disabilities. (4) Where etched or patterned glass is being used, decals or stripes shall be of highly contrasting colours from the base. (5) A partially glazed door shall have a glazed panel that extends low at a maximum height from grade 900mm to lower edge of glazing, in order to allow a person in a sitting position view the far side of the door, as specified Figure 2.014 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (6) Installation of a door at a doorway shall conform to the specifications in Table 2.2 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (7) A self-closing hinged or pivoted door across a passageway, which can be pushed to open in both directions, shall conform to the following -- (a) have controlled door closing devices, and allow for independent use ; (b) a self-closing hinged or pivoted door, other than an entrance door across a passageway, shall have a viewing panel ; and (c) a self-closing hinged or pivoted door on an escape route shall conform to the requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering. (8) Glass doors may be used across passageways, provided that they shall conform to the following— (a) a glass door or a fully glazed door with a narrow stile shall — (i) be visible, with permanent manifestation within two zones measuring from 850mm to 1000mm from the floor and from 1400mm to 1600mm from the floor, and (ii) contrast visually with the background seen through the glass in all light conditions ; (b) the edges of a glass door shall be framed on both sides and the top, by an opaque high-contrast strip measuring a minimum width of 25mm to ensure that the door is visible ; (c) where a glass door is adjacent to or is incorporated within a fully glazed wall, the door shall be prominent, and clearly differentiated from the wall ; and (d) a glazed door should conform to the requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering. (9) An architrave or frame lacking an architrave shall contrast visually with a wall surface surrounding the doorway. (10) Where double doors of unequal width are used along the length of a passageway, the broader leaf shall be on the same side of the passageway throughout its length. (11) A cross passageway fire-resisting door shall conform to the requirements set out in sub-regulations (9) and (10) of this regulation. (12) A fire-resisting door shall be fitted with a controlled door closing device, irrespective of whether the door is latched or unlatched. (13) For the purposes of this regulation — (a) “self-closing hinged door” means a single swing door ; and (b) “pivoted door” means a single or double swing door that is hinged from the bottom and top of a door.

regs.title: Cupboard door hardware.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 98. —(1) Door pulls or latches shall be of the lever handle or Simple ‘D’ type for easy use by persons with disabilities. (2) Door hardware shall be mounted at a height not exceeding 1065mm. (3) Where practicable, a handle shall be part of a lockset. (4) Sliding cupboard or door hardware shall be mounted so that the remaining clear door opening is a minimum width of 860mm, as specified in Figure 2.016 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Cupboard unit door and drawer handles shall be easy to grip. (6) Cupboard unit doors shall swing open through 180° to allow for easy and unrestricted access. (7) Where there is a shared kitchen facility, door pulls of high-level wall cupboards shall be positioned towards the bottom of the door. (8) Sliding doors and drawers shall be capable of being operated with limited force when operated from the front or side.

regs.title: Mats and mat sinkages.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 99. —(1) Mats at entrances and in vestibules shall — (a) be level with the floor surface ; (b) be located in mat sinkages ; and (c) have gently beveled edges, so as not to constitute a tripping hazard, as specified in Figure 2.017 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Where a runner mat is used to define preferred walking routes or give directions, it shall lead directly to the target area, and the runner mat shall be clear of any obstacle intruding into the route. (3) Runner mats shall be as continuous as possible, and in a contrasting colour or tone to the adjacent floor. (4) A floor covering with large or repeating patterns that incorporate bold contrasting colours or simulate steps shall not be used on a floor surface.

regs.title: Thresholds.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 100. —(1) Thresholds shall be beveled, and not exceed a height of 13mm, where they are— (a) located at interior doorways ; or (b) required to accommodate floor level or finished changes to exterior areas. (2) An existing or altered threshold with a maximum height of 19mm, which has a beveled edge on each side, shall have a slope not steeper than 1 : 2. (3) An entrance threshold — (a) may be level ; or (b) where a raised threshold is unavoidable, such as to prevent water ingress, shall have one or more upstands and slopes, provided that the cumulative height of such upstands shall not exceed 15mm. (4) An upstand that measures more than 5mm in height, shall have exposed edges, which may be chamfered or pencil rounded. (5) Thresholds to internal doors shall be leveled at a junctions with different flooring materials. (6) The provisions of sub-regulation (1) of this regulation shall be, as specified in Figure 2.020 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Vestibules.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 101. —(1) An interior vestibule shall measure a minimum width of 1100mm to allow for easy navigation and turns at right angles through door openings. (2) The depth of a vestibule shall be — (a) a minimum width of 1200mm floor space to allow for the maneuvering of mobility aids ; and (b) clear of door swings and other obstacles. (3) Where a door swings towards a person using mobility aid, a minimum clear space of 600mm shall be available at the jamb, on the opening edge of the door, to ensure easy access to the door, as specified in Figure 2.018 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Where a door swings away from a person using a mobility aid, a minimum clear space of 300mm shall be available adjacent to the jamb on the opening edge of the door to ensure easy access, as specified in Figure 2.019 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Waiting areas.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 102. —(1) A waiting area shall be leveled, and large enough to — (a) accommodate a minimum of two wheelchairs users, furniture and other members of the public ; and (b) allow persons using mobility aids to manoeuver. (2) Seating furniture in a general waiting area in public and commercial buildings shall — (a) measure between 450mm and 475mm in height ; and (b) have arm rest or side supports. (3) The provisions of subsection (2) of this regulation, shall not apply to seating furniture in closely seated public and commercial buildings such as auditorium, theatre, and cinema.

regs.title: Seating layouts.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 103. —(1) A seating layout shall be designed to — (a) contain persons, including a minimum of two wheelchair users sitting next to each other ; and (b) allow space, the size of a standard seat, within or at the end of a block of seating for an assistance dog. (2) Where practicable, a mixture of fixed and removable seats may be provided to accommodate different seating layouts. (3) In this regulation “assistance dog” include guide dogs and hearing dogs.

regs.title: Interior circulation routes.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 104. Interior circulation routes of a public building such as, passage ways shall — (a) be wide enough to accommodate movement of persons, including persons using mobility aids ; (b) except otherwise stated, have no unexpected level changes, and be free of obstruction ; (c) have handrail support or resting place, where the internal circulation route is long ; and (d) make provision for seats at intermediate points along the passageway, where the internal circulation route exceeds a length of 40,000mm.

regs.title: Aisles and passageways.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 105. —(1) In a low use public area such as a small office, a small hotel, and other buildings of like capacity, a clear aisle space or passageway between walls, glazed screen, furniture, or other fixed obstacle shall be a minimum width of 1200mm to accommodate the movement of a person, including a wheelchair user, as specified in Figures 2.020 and 2.021 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) In high use public area such as a mall, big hotel, hospital and other buildings of like capacity, a clear aisle, or passageway between walls shall be a minimum width of 1675mm to accommodate a minimum of two wheelchair users, as specified in Figure 2.021 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) Subject to sub regulation (1) of this regulation, where an aisle with a width of 1200mm is extensive in length or terminates in a dead-end, a turning space measuring a minimum length of 1600mm and minimum width of 1600mm shall be provided at 30000mm intervals and dead-end locations. (4) In a high use public area, a passageway shall be a minimum width of 1675mm, and have a turning space of 1600mm in diameter, at every 20000mm interval, to permit the free movement, including a person using mobility aid as specified in Figure 2.022 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Projections into aisles and passageways.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 106. —(1) A circulation route shall be free of obstruction, such as dust bin, radiator, fire extinguisher, or fire hose, provided that where an obstruction is fixed or required, the obstruction shall be guarded, as specified in Figure 2.023 and 2.024 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Subject to sub regulation (1) of this regulation, an obstruction at the end of a circulation route shall be clearly marked with a warning sign, provided at the start of the route. (3) Artificial lighting in a passageway shall be even, diffused and without glare, reflections or shadows, provided that artificial lighting for a passageway that receive no daylight shall be have illuminance at floor level of a minimum of 100lux.

regs.title: Doors across passageways.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 107. Doors across passageways shall comply with the provisions of regulation 85 of these Regulations.

regs.title: Fire escape routes via horizontal circulation.
regs.header: 108. Fire escape routes via horizontal circulation.
regs.arrangement_title: Fire escape routes via horizontal circulation
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 108. —(1) An unobstructed passageway leading to an escape route, shall be a minimum width of 1200mm. (2) Escape routes shall conform to the requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering.

regs.title: Lifts.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 109. —(1) Lifts for use in a public building may be conventional passenger lifts, vertical lifting platforms, or stair-lifts. (2) Where practicable, a public building with an existing stairway may be fitted with a non-enclosed lifting platforms to transfer a wheelchair user on a guarded platform vertically from one level to another. (3) Lifts shall be designed to be accessible to persons using mobility aids. (4) A lift shall — (a) be equipped with an audio floor announcing feature ; (b) have tactile controls or buttons, which are easy to reach and operate ; (c) be fitted with a concave mirror installed at the back of the lift car ; (d) be equipped with lighting, which illumination shall be a minimum of 100lux measured at the floor level ; (e) be equipped with an emergency call system, with 2-way voice communication capability and an SMS facility, linked to a monitored location within the building ; (f ) have non-slip floor surface, and comply with the provisions of these Regulations relating to floor surfaces ; and (g) comply with the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering. (5) Adjacent lobby space at the lift entrance shall be equipped with lighting, which illumination shall be a minimum of 100lux measured at the floor level. (6) A high-rise public residential building and public building shall be equipped with a lift of a minimum platform size measuring 1725mm by 2285mm, as specified in Figure 2.025 and 2.045 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Passenger lift.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 110. A passenger lift shall comply with the following requirements— (a) a lift keypad or information system call buttons, keypads, or SMS facilities shall be raised ; (b) call buttons and keypads on a passenger lift shall be located as prescribed in Table 2.3 of the First Schedule of these Regulations ; (c) call buttons, SMS facility, and keypads shall be located at a maximum height of 1370mm above the finished floor, measured to the centre line of the highest operable part ; and (d) the size of a call button shall be a minimum width of 19mm in the smallest dimension.

regs.title: Platform lifts.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 111. —(1) A platform lift shall not be attendant-operated, and provide unassisted entry and exit from the lift. (2) Entrance to a platform lift shall have a vertical clearance of 2030mm. (3) The clearance between the platform sill and the edge of any runway landing shall measure a maximum width of 32mm. (4) A platform lift shall have low-energy power-operated doors or gates. (5) A platform lift serving a maximum of two landings and having doors or gates on opposite sides shall have self-closing manual doors or gates. (6) A platform lift shall have a clear width of— (a) 815mm, in the case of a lift with end doors and gates ; or (b) 1065mm, in the case of a lift with a side door and gate, as specified in Figures 2.026, 2.027 and 2.028 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Interior ramps.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 112. —(1) Where there are minimal elevations within a building, an interior ramp shall be provided instead of a platform lift. (2) An interior ramp shall have a maximum slope of 1 : 15, as specified in Figure 1.021, 1.022, 1.023 and 1,024 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Lighting platforms or daises.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 113. Lighting platforms or daises provided for display or presentation purposes shall be accessible to and useable by persons with mobility aids.

regs.title: Safe holding areas.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 114. —(1) Where a safe holding area is included as part of the emergency plan for persons with disabilities, such holding area shall— (a) be able to accommodate, among other persons, persons using mobility aids ; (b) be located on each floor, above or below grade, which is easy to identify by persons with visual disabilities and be accessible to persons using mobility aids ; (c) have separate emergency lighting and ventilation systems ; and (d) have a two-way voice communication system linked to the fire control centre. (2) Safe holding area within a stair lobby, passageway, or room adjacent to a stairway, shall be provided in accordance with the requirement relevant to the British Standard Code of Engineering.

regs.title: Stairs and steps.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 115. Stairs and steps within a building shall conform with the provisions of regulation 15 of these Regulations.

regs.title: Turnstiles and control gates.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 116. —(1) Where turnstiles or other crowd control gates are used to manage the movement of people, the turnstiles shall — (a) be of a breakaway design to accommodate persons using wheelchairs or scooters ; or (b) have an adjacent access gate that is wide enough to allow the passage of persons using mobility aids. (2) Clearances at turnstiles or gates shall measure a minimum clear width of 860mm.

regs.title: Access to interior amenities.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 117. Interior amenities shall be accessible by persons with disabilities.

regs.title: Hanging racks.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 118. —(1) Hanging racks shall be provided on every floor in a public building, and a 10 per cent of the hanging rack shall be reserved for and accessible to persons with disabilities (2) A hanging rack shall have coat rods or coat hooks fixed securely and mounted at a height between 1200mm and 1370mm (3) Clear door opening for closets fitted with a hanging rack shall measure a minimum width of 810mm to allow a frontal approach by persons using mobility aids. (4) Where a public building or facility provides a public check-in counter for the storage of personal items, a section of the counter shall be lowered to comply with regulation 84 of these Regulations.

regs.title: Drinking fountains.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 119. —(1) Drinking fountains shall be accessible to persons with disabilities. (2) Drinking fountains shall be set to one side of the path of travel with enough approach room for persons using mobility aids as specified in Figure 2.030 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) A wall-mounted or recessed drinking fountain shall have a clear knee space measuring a width of 765mm and a height of 735mm at the underside of the fountain. (4) Controls for the drinking fountain shall be— (a) mounted to one side of the bowl ; (b) of a maximum height of 915mm ; and (c) operable with one hand. (5) The spout for water projection shall measure a maximum height of 915mm, with a trajectory across the bowl as specified in Figure 2.030 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Equipment and furniture.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 120. —(1) The layout of furniture or equipment in the interior of a public building shall not constitute a hazard. (2) Furniture, equipment, facilities, and planters, shall be positioned at the same side of the normal path of travel. (3) Open seating such as a chair or bench shall measure between 405mm and 460mm in height. (4) Seats with armrests and backrests shall be provided for persons with disabilities. (5) Tables and desks shall be provided with a working surface measuring a maximum height of 785mm, minimum width of 760mm between supports, and a clear knee space height of 700mm, as specified in Figure 2.031 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (6) Planters with strong cane-detectable bases shall be used as specified in Figure 2.095 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Storage facilities.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 121. —(1) Where in a public building storage compartments are being used, 10 per cent of the storage compartments shall be reserved for use by persons with disabilities. (2) A storage compartment reserved for persons with disabilities shall — (a) have the bottom shelf of the compartment measuring a maximum height of 1220mm and a minimum height of 460mm, from the floor ; (b) measure a minimum width of 300mm and a maximum depth of 600mm ; and (c) have a base set between 400mm and 800mm above floor level, as specified in Figures 2.035 and 2.036 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) subject to sub-regulation (2) of this regulation, a lock fitted for storage compartment shall be — (a) mounted at height of 915mm from the ground, but not higher than 1065mm ; and (b) easy to operate, one-handed, by persons with disabilities. (4) Information inscribed on a storage compartment referred to in sub- regulation (2) of this regulation, such as name, number, or other information, shall be— (a) mounted at a maximum height of 1525mm ; (b) in distinct and legible lettering ; and (c) on raised or recessed lettering format, and the colour of the lettering shall be highly contrasted from the background. (5) Subject to sub-regulation (4) of this regulation, the size of the lettering or number shall be between 13mm and 19mm in height. (6) A projecting door and drawer hardware of a storage facility shall contrast with the storage compartment and have no sharp edges. (7) A storage compartment shall — (a) contrast visually with its surroundings ; (b) not have highly reflective surfaces ; and (c) where practicable, be provided adequate lighting, as specified in Figure 2.037 and 2.038 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (8) A compartment or carousel for luggage shall have a platform surface of a maximum height of 460mm from the floor.

regs.title: Access to storage facilities.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 122. —(1) Access to a storage facility shall be direct, free from obstruction, and where practicable, have sufficient space to allow free movement on the front and from the side, by person in a wheelchair. (2) Where practicable, a storage facility shall be equipped with seats for persons with disabilities. (3) The aisle clearance between opposing banks of storage compartments, such as a shelf storage units, filing cabinets or locker shall be a minimum width of — (a) 1200mm, if knee space is provided ; or (b) 1400mm, if no knee space is provided. (4) Aisle space in front of a storage compartment or carousel shall measure a minimum depth of 1370mm to permit the forward or lateral approach by a person using mobility aid. (5) Where practicable, a storage compartment shall be fitted with adjustable fixtures and fittings to ensure easy access by persons with disabilities.

regs.title: Mailboxes.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 123. The provisions of regulation 36 of these Regulations shall apply with regard to mailboxes located within public buildings..

regs.title: Mirrors.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 124. —(1) Mirrors located in public restrooms and bathrooms shall be available, and mounted at a height to enable for use by persons in wheelchairs. (2) Subject to sub regulation (1) of this regulation, a mirror shall be mounted at a height such that the lower edge of the mirror over a washbasin measures a maximum height of 915mm from the floor, as specified in Figures 2.039 and 2.040 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) Notwithstanding the provisions of sub regulation (2) of this regulation, where it is not practicable to mount a mirror over a washbasin, a public restroom or bathroom shall be provided with a separate full-length mirror. (4) Subject to sub regulation (3) of this regulation, a full-length mirror shall be mounted — (a) at a height such that the lower edge of the mirror measure a height of 610mm from the floor and extend not less than 1830mm in height ; and (b) where there is a clear floor area at a depth of 915mm by 1370mm in front of the mirror to ensure easy access by persons using mobility aids.

regs.title: Restrooms and washrooms.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 125. The provisions of regulations 59 to 62 of these Regulations shall apply with regard to restrooms and washrooms located indoors.

regs.title: Work surface layout in a work station.
regs.header: 126. Work surface layout in a work station.
regs.arrangement_title: Work surface layout in a work station
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 126. —(1) Except as expressly mentioned, a work surface shall be designed in an “L” or “U” shape, and where practicable, be continuous. (2) There shall be a smooth transition between a work surface and other sections in a work station. (3) Where in a self-catering kitchen or self-catering accommodation in a public residential building, occupied by persons using wheelchairs and other persons, the work surface of the kitchen shall be of two different maximum height levels of 760mm and 900mm, as specified in Figure 2.032 and 2.033 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) A work surface shall be of a maximum depth of 600mm and provide knee recesses with reduced work surface depth to allow wheelchair users reach over the work surface. (5) Where practicable, work surfaces may be adjustable. (6) The front edge of the work surface shall have a rounded profile.

regs.title: Work surface accessories.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 127. —(1) Where in a kitchen or workshop, circulation space is limited making it difficult to have an accessible work surface, pull-out boards shall be provided as a supplementary accessible work surface. (2) A pull-out board shall — (a) be fitted in a manner so as not to restrict the movement of users over a work surface ; (b) be finished with rubber beading ; and (c) contrast visually with the background when left in the "out" position.

regs.title: Vending machines.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 128. Where a vending machine is provided indoors — (a) controls, dispensing areas, or other working parts shall be located at a maximum height of 1200mm and at a minimum height of 465mm from the floor ; (b) signage on a vending machine shall be in high contrast letters, and at a minimum height of 13mm ; and (c) the floor space in front of vending machines shall be a minimum length of 1370mm by 1525mm, as specified in Figures 2.042 and 2.043 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Windows and window hardware.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 129. —(1) In a building designed with operable windows— (a) the opening section of the windows shall be at a maximum sill height of 760mm from the floor ; (b) windows with horizontal transoms shall be mounted at a height between 1070mm and 1200mm ; and (c) window opening hardware shall be mounted at a maximum height of 1065mm, as specified in Figure 2.044 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Window hardware shall be designed to be operated one-handed, with lever action and not twist or rotary action. (3) Windows in a public residential building shall be designed to deflect direct drafts away from an occupant when opened.

regs.title: Acoustic attenuating features.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 130. —(1) Building materials that create echo sounds shall not be used in the construction of a public building. (2) Where practicable, a public address or call system shall be located in critical areas of a building. (3) Subject to sub regulation (1) of this regulation, building materials shall conform with the requirements of the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering.

regs.title: Audible and visual information.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 131. —(1) Essential audible signals, such as fire-alarm signals or elevator arrival call systems, shall be loud and distinct enough to be heard at a minimum of 15 decibels louder than the ambient sound as specified in Figure 2.046 and 2.047 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Fire alarm signals in public buildings shall be designed with both visual and audio features.

regs.title: Communication systems.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 132. —(1) General, non-emergency, communication systems shall be accessible, useable and understood by persons with disabilities. (2) A two-way communication system with voice input or output provided in a building shall include visual display. (3) Communication systems, such as telephones, SMS facility relay and intercoms, shall be equipped with volume enhancement, and where practicable, hearing loops for persons using hearing aids. (4) Where practicable, information counters, enquiry and booking locations, may provide for the use of a TTY telephone, as specified in Figure 2.048 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Signs that are designed to be read by touch shall not have sharp or abrasive edges. (6) Characters contained in a communication system shall be— (a) raised, and with a minimum height measuring 0.8mm above the background ; and (b) bold and in uppercase font.

regs.title: Braille.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 133. Braille dots shall have a domed or rounded shape, and comply with Table 2.5, and Figures 2.049 and 2.050 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Symbols of accessibility.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 134. —(1) Symbols of accessibility and their background shall have a non- glare finish. (2) Symbols of accessibility shall contrast with their background as specified in Figure 1.033 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Controls and electrical installations.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 135. —(1) Switches and controls within a building shall be easy to locate, operate and free from obstruction. (2) Where applicable, a photo-luminescent pictogram sign shall be deployed to indicate or locate controls or operating mechanisms. (3) Except as expressly mentioned, a control device shall be installed between 460mm and 1100mm above floor level, and be located at a minimum of 600mm away from the entrance or approach. (4) A control device containing text or figures, or both shall be positioned at the angle of approximately 45° to the wall to ensure that the contents are easy to read and device easy to operate, such as, a panel in an elevator. (5) A control device placed on a horizontal surface shall be placed at a height between 800mm and 900mm, and 300mm away from the edge of the surface. (6) Subject to sub regulation (4) of this regulation, a control device shall be— (a) located between a minimum height of 400mm and maximum height of 1000mm from the floor, in the case of socket outlets ; and (b) mounted at a maximum height of 1200mm, in the case of light switches, thermostats and security controls. (7) Controls and operating mechanisms shall be of a distinct colour or tone from the background. (8) Information detailing the use or operation of controls or operating mechanisms shall be — (a) in large print text on a highly contrasting background ; and (b) mounted close to a control or operating mechanism. (9) A raised pushbutton control shall be a minimum width of 13mm in diameter. (10) The provisions of this regulation shall be, as specified in Figure 2.051 and 2.052 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Electrical power supply.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 136. —(1) Electrical power design shall allow for supplementary lighting and communication devices to be added, where necessary. (2) A public building shall provide emergency power to accommodate emergency and other vital operating components such as lighting levels, and lifts.

regs.title: Fire emergency systems and signals.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 137. —(1) Fire alarm systems shall be designed and installed in accordance with the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering. (2) A fire alarm signal shall— (a) be visible, as well as audible to users ; (b) mounted high on the a wall ; and (c) be easily visible against background colour and lighting. (3) Fire alarm signal shall have — (a) visible flashing signals ; and (b) a distinctive sounds with two-stage evacuation distinguishable from each other in each stage as specified in Figure 2. 045 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Fire-exiting announcement procedures shall be loud enough to be heard above ambient noise levels, and be preceded by a distinctive sound, in order to alert building occupants. (5) The pulse of visible flashing signals shall be tested to ensure that it does not trigger epileptic seizures. (6) A portable vibratory alarm shall be provided to supplement visual signals for persons, with disabilities.

regs.title: HVAC and cooling systems.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 138. —(1) Heating, cooling and ventilation systems shall be designed to accommodate persons whose respiratory systems are inadequate. (2) Facilities serving persons with disabilities shall be designed to operate between— (a) 21º C and 26º C temperature at all times of the year ; and (b) 30 per cent—40 per cent humidity in the air. (3) Mechanical ventilation and air-cooling systems shall not be mounted to allow the airflow from diffusers or grills to be directed towards a person lying in bed, seating, or working locations. (4) Air handling system shall be mounted to be acoustically isolated to minimize noise.

regs.title: Information systems and directories.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 139. —(1) Information systems providing direct information to the public shall be comprehensible to persons with disabilities as specified in regulation 132 of these Regulations. (2) Where auditory information is available, it shall be complemented by suitable printed material. (3) Information on visual display screens shall be available in other formats, including audiotape or large print. (4) Enlarged font shall be used on display monitors. (5) Lighting levels at keyboards and other controls shall be evenly distributed at a minimum of 200lux intensity. (6) Visual display screens in public information shall be mounted to ensure that there is no direct glare on the surface of the screen.

regs.title: Artificial lighting.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 140. —(1) Artificial lighting shall be installed— (a) on the floors of all circulation routes ; and (b) in all areas of potential hazard. (2) Light sources and fixtures shall minimize direct and indirect glare from nearby reflective surfaces for users to navigate safely. (3) Lighting shall be designed to ensure that the quality of light is close to a full spectrum. (4) Light colour temperature between 27000K and 30000K shall be used to offset fluorescent or quartz light sources with a high blue content. (5) Light fixtures with multiple points of high-intensity light shall not be used. (6) The leading edges of stairs, steps, ramps, or escalators shall be evenly lit to minimize tripping hazards. (7) Lighting levels in an lift or elevator lobby shall — (a) be similar to the lighting levels in a lift or elevator cab in order to minimize tripping hazards ; and (b) measure a minimum of 100lux intensity at the threshold of the elevator. (8) Where practicable, emergency lighting over interior stairs and ramps, in exits or other paths of travel shall measure 100lux intensity at the walking surface and 50lux intensity at the exterior locations. (9) Lighting over directional or informational signage such as at public telephones, informational or service counters, automated teller machines, or other keypad operations, shall measure a minimum of 200lux intensity at the working or information surface. (10) Lighting over lecterns, podiums, platforms, or other speaker locations shall be capable of being enhanced, even when other lighting points are dimmed, to permit lip-reading and a view of any of the hand actions used to communicate. (11) An artificial lighting system shall — (a) be designed to be compatible with electronic and radio frequency installations ; and (b) use high-frequency electronic ballasts to avoid any perception of flicker. (12) Where practicable, uplighters with a light source at the floor or low level shall not be used as they cause glare and obscure vision.

regs.title: Natural lighting.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 141.—(1) Where practicable, natural light shall be utilized to assist in lighting entrances, passageway and major workspaces, and care shall be taken to minimize direct glare. (2) Natural lighting shall be utilized in accordance with the relevant British Standard Code of Engineering.

regs.title: Listening devices.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 142. —(1) An FM loop or other assistive listening systems shall be — (a) provided at meeting rooms, assembly and entertainment areas, serving more than 35 persons ; and (b) provided with portable headsets compatible with personal hearing aids ; as specified in Figure 2.055 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) Where infrared assistive listening devices are used, overhead lights shall not intercept infrared signal at the receiver. (3) Dimmer switches and other transformer coils in meeting areas, shall be carefully located to prevent electromagnetic interference with any audio induction loop. (4) Where an induction loop system is utilized, only half of the seating area shall be encompassed. (5) A theatre or studio intended for viewing of motion pictures shall accommodate described video and the installation of rear-view captioning, in compliance with the Nigerian NBC. (6) Larger meeting rooms shall be designed and furnished to allow a clear view of the speaker at all times.

regs.title: Assistive listening systems.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 143. —(1) In each assembly area where audible communication is integral to the use of the space, an assistive listening system shall be provided. (2) Receivers shall be provided for assistive listening systems in each assembly area as specified in Table 2.6 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) Where all seats in an assembly area are served by an induction loop assistive listening system, the minimum number of receivers shall be as specified in Table 2.6 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Public address systems.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 144. —(1) A public address system shall be — (a) easy to hear above ambient background noise, without distortion or feedback ; and (b) zoned to allow the direction of information to key locations only. (2) A public address speaker shall — (a) be mounted above head-level ; and (b) provide adequate sound coverage in required areas. (3) All-point call systems shall only be utilized for fire and emergency information. (4) Personal alarm, and staff or other call systems shall be — (a) selected with care and according to the requirements of the particular setting or user ; and (b) used with discretion. (5) Paging systems for use by staff or other key personnel shall be— (a) be discreet and low in volume ; and (b) only sound at locations, where such persons might reasonably be expected to be located.

regs.title: Telephones.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 145. The provisions of regulations 65 and 132 of these Regulations shall apply to this regulation and as specified in Figure 2.056 of First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Signage and way-finding.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 146. The provisions of regulation 69 of these Regulations shall apply to this regulation.

regs.title: Automated Teller Machines (ATMs).
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 147. —(1) ATMs shall be designed to be accessible for persons with disabilities. (2) An ATM shall have a clear floor space in front and underneath it, measuring a minimum depth of 1220mm and minimum width of 915mm, and knee space height of 685mm, as specified in Figure 2.062 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) ATM controls, switches, panels, and card, coin, and cash location, shall be mounted at a maximum height of 1000mm from the floor level. (4) Control buttons, and coin or card access locations on an ATM shall— (a) be easily identifiable ; (b) have tactile features, and raised numbers or letters ; and (c) be distinctively coloured. (5) An ATM shall be equipped with — (a) audio accessibility devices to provide voice or sound cues or instructions ; and (b) volume controls for persons with hearing disabilities.

regs.title: Ticketing machines.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 148. —(1) Ticketing machines for parking, fares, admission, and general services shall be accessible to persons with disabilities. (2) Operable or dispensing parts of a ticketing machine shall measure a maximum height of 1200mm and minimum height of 915mm, from floor level. (3) Control buttons, and coin or card access locations shall — (a) be easily identifiable ; (b) have tactile features, and raised numbers or letters ; and (c) be distinctively coloured.

regs.title: Video and image display terminals.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 149. The provisions of regulation 139, 142, and 143 of these Regulations shall apply with regard to video and image display terminals.

regs.title: Restaurants and other eateries.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 150. —(1) A restaurant or other eating area offering food services to the public shall be accessible to persons with disabilities. (2) Aisle spaces between furniture, equipment, or other fixed objects shall measure a minimum width of 900mm, as specified in Figure 2.066 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) A reception area or information desk, and cashier point of a restaurant or other eating area shall comply with the provisions of regulation 84 of these Regulations. (4) A restaurant or other eating area, where food services are provided shall conform to the following — (a) food displays shall be mounted on a surface with a minimum height of 915mm from the floor ; and (b) overhead display shelves shall measure a maximum height of 1220mm from floor level, as specified in Figure 2.035 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (5) Drink dispensing areas shall comply with the provisions of regulation 119 of these Regulations.

regs.title: Place of Worship.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 151. —(1) Places of worship including main areas of worship, meeting rooms, restrooms and bathrooms, and offices shall be accessible to persons with disabilities. (2) Seating areas or praying spaces within a place of worship shall comply with regulation 54 of these Regulations. (3) Notwithstanding the provisions of sub-regulation (2) of this regulation, a minimum of 8 per cent of seats or praying spaces in a place of worship shall be reserved for persons with disabilities. (4) Ablution area or spaces shall be accessible to persons with disabilities, and conform to bathroom specification prescribed in regulation 59 to 64 of these Regulations.

regs.title: Public institutions in the criminal justice system.
regs.header: 152. Public institutions in the criminal justice system.
regs.arrangement_title: Public institutions in the criminal justice system
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 152. Public institutions such as a court, police station, or correctional center shall ensure that information is provided in accessible format as set out in these Regulations.

regs.title: Health Care and social welfare facilities.
regs.header: 153. Health Care and social welfare facilities.
regs.arrangement_title: Health Care and social welfare facilities
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 153. A facility that provides healthcare or social welfare services to the public shall be accessible to persons with disabilities, as prescribed under these Regulations.

regs.title: Libraries.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 154. —(1) A facility that provides library services to the public shall be accessible to persons with disabilities, as prescribed under these Regulations. (2) Book return and checking area counters shall conform to the provisions of regulation 84(3)(4), (7)-(9) of these Regulations. (3) Book shelves shall have an aisle space measuring a minimum width of 1065mm, as specified in Figure 2.063 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) Lighting at book shelves shall be mounted directly over the aisle space and provide a minimum of 200lux at normal working height of 915mm. (5) Study tables shall measure a maximum depth of 600mm, and provide knee space with a minimum height of 700mm. (6) Shelves constructed over study tables shall be of a maximum height of 1000mm from the table.

regs.title: Schools and Education Centres.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 155. Schools and other education centres shall comply with the provisions of these Regulations.

regs.title: Public residence.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 156. —(1) A public residence shall comply with the provisions of these Regulations. (2) A public residence shall be equipped with a fire alarm system, which wiring system shall be connected to a smoke detection system. (3) Fire alarm system in a public residence shall comply with the provisions of regulation 137 of these Regulations. (4) The main entrance of a public residence shall be equipped with — (a) communication features, which shall include a two-way communication system, and where practicable, a visual display screen ; (b) a hard-wired electric doorbell, which shall— (i) initiate an audible tone and visible signal, and (ii) have controls to deactivate the signal, where the bell is located in sleeping areas. (5) An entrance door to a residential unit of a public residence shall be fitted with a peep hole that allows for a minimum of 180-degree range of view and clarifies the image in view. (6) Where a residential unit of a public residence that is designed to be accessible is located on— (a) an upper floor, it shall be located close to a lift ; or (b) the ground floor, it shall be located close to the reception area or main entrance.

regs.title: Kitchen in a public residence.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 157. —(1) A kitchen in a public residence shall comply with the provisions of these Regulation, and in particular— (a) have an aisle between counters with a minimum width of 1065mm ; (b) where practicable, have a turning space in dead-end areas, with a minimum width of 1500mm ; and (c) have clear knee space below counters, as specified in Figures 2.069, 2.070, 2.071, and 2.072 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (2) A kitchen stove may be fitted with front or side regulator control, or where practicable, an automatic switch control. (3) A clear counter space with a minimum width of 300mm shall be provided on both sides of a stove to ensure safe operation. (4) Where a cabinet is located under a work surface— (a) the cabinet shall be capable of being removed without tampering with, removing, or replacing the kitchen work surface ; (b) the finished floor shall extend under the cabinet ; and (c) the wall behind and surrounding the cabin shall be finished.

regs.title: Special washroom in a public residence.
regs.header: 158. Special washroom in a public residence.
regs.arrangement_title: Special washroom in a public residence
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 158. —(1) A residential unit of a public residence that is designed to be accessible may comply with the provisions of this regulation. (2) A washroom that incorporates a corner water closet layout for independent use shall be as specified in Figures 2.077 and 2.078 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (3) A washroom equipped with a ceiling-mounted full room cover, tracked hoist system for assisted service shall be as specified in Figure 2.075 of the First Schedule to these Regulations. (4) A washroom allowing for — (a) assisted use of a bath, without hoist, and a peninsular water closet shall be as specified in Figure 2.073 and Figure 2.078 of the First Schedule to these Regulations ; or (b) assisted use of the bath and WC, with space for a mobile hoist operated by an assistant, shall be as specified in Figures 2.078 and 2.079 of the First Schedule to these Regulations.

regs.title: Bedroom in a public residence.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 159. —(1) A bedroom in a public residence shall comply with the provisions of these Regulations. (2) Where a public residence has provision for an accessible bedroom, the bedroom— (a) may be furnished with en-suite toilet and bathroom facility ; (b) shall be capable of being adapted to suit accessibility needs ; (c) shall be free from obstruction ; (d) shall be located close to the entrance door ; (e) have a clearance space measuring a minimum length of 1500mm and minimum width of 1500mm on one side of a bed ; (f ) shall be furnished with a bed— (i) which frame shall measure a maximum height of 480mm from floor level, an a minimum clearance under the bed of 150mm, and (ii) which shall not have extra legs midway between the corner legs ; (h) shall be furnished with a firm mattress ; and (i) may be equipped with under-pillow vibrating units or vibrating under- mattress pads that plug into the fire alarm system. (3) Furniture and fittings in a bedroom shall contrast with their surroundings. (4) Notwithstanding the provisions of sub-regulation (2)(a) of this regulation to furnish an accessible room with an en-suite toilet and bathroom provided shall comply with the provisions of these Regulations.

regs.title: Shops and shopping malls.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 160. —(1) Shop, shopping malls, and other building where goods and services are provided shall comply with the provisions of these Regulations. (2) A shopping mall shall provide close to its entrance, a drop off or setting- down point. (3) The drop off or setting-down point referred to in sub-regulation (2) of this regulation shall have a raised kerb, which runs along the length of the drop off or setting-down point bay width.

regs.title: Accessible cabin coach.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 161. —(1) A train shall have a minimum of one accessible cabin coach. (2) An accessible cabin shall — (a) have an accessible restroom, (b) be equipped with an on-board wheelchair ; and (c) have an aisle measuring a width of 900mm.

regs.title: Life safety plan.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 162. A building shall, at its entrance, provide an evacuation plan and mustering strategies.

regs.title: Maintenance.
regs.chapter: CHAPTER THREE—REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERIOR OR INDOOR AREAS
regs.text: 163. A person to whom these Regulations apply under regulation 2 of these Regulations shall develop a maintenance manual for use.

regs.title: Inter-agency collaboration.
regs.text: 164. The Commission shall collaborate with relevant MDAs and professional bodies to ensure compliance with the provisions of these Regulations.

regs.title: Compliance procedures.
regs.text: 165. —(1) A person to whom these Regulations apply under regulation 2 of these Regulations shall, prior to a new construction, present a construction plan to the relevant authority to ensure that the plan conforms with the standards and code for an accessible built environment, as set out in these Regulations. (2) The Commission may issue a provisional accessibility compliance certificate, where satisfied that the relevant authority approved the construction plan submitted under sub-regulation (1) of this regulation. (3) The Commission shall conduct an accessibility audit on a built environment existing prior to the commencement of these Regulations upon the expiration of 21 days accessibility audit notice issued by the Commission to an owner or occupier of the built environment. (4) The Commission may issue a National Accessibility Compliance Certificate— (a) where satisfied that a built environment referred to in sub-regulation (3) of this regulation complies with the provisions of these Regulations ; and (b) on the payment of prescribed assessment fees, as may be determined by the Commission. (5) A National Accessibility Compliance Certificate issued by the Commission shall be valid for a period of five years. (6) The Commission shall monitor compliance of these Regulations, and report any non-compliance to — (a) the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, in the case of an MDA ; and (b) a relevant authority, in the case of a person under regulation 2 of these Regulations, other than an MDA.

regs.title: National Disability Compliance Certificate.
regs.text: 166. —(1) A person to whom these Regulations apply under regulation 2 of these Regulations shall, from the commencement of these Regulations, apply to the Commission for the National Disability Compliance Certificate. (2) The Commission shall issue a National Disability Compliance Certificate where it is satisfied— (a) that an applicant has completed the certification course referred to in regulation 167 of these Regulations ; (b) with an applicant’s compliance with the provisions of the Act and these Regulations ; and (c) that an applicant has paid the prescribed fees. (3) A National Disability Compliance Certificate shall be valid for a period of one year. (4) The Commission shall issue a penalty on the renewal of a National Disability Compliance Certificate where a person fails to renew the certificate within 90 days of its expiration. (5) The Commission may withdraw a Certificate issued under this regulation, where it was obtained contrary to regulation 167(2) of these Regulations. (6) The National Disability Compliance Certificate is a mandatory pre- qualification document for biddingon procurement of public works, goods, and services.

regs.title: Capacity building on accessibility and compli- ance.
regs.header: 167. Capacity building on accessibility and compli- ance.
regs.arrangement_title: Capacity building on accessibility and compliance
regs.text: 167. —(1) The Commission may, by itself, conduct or approve the conduct of a certification course on accessibility and inclusive development. (2) The attendance and completion of the certification course referred to in sub-regulation (1) of this regulation is mandatory and a condition for the issuance of a National Disability Compliance Certificate. (3) The certification course referred to in sub-regulation (1) of this regulation and the National Disability Compliance Certificate issued by the Commission shall be mandatory requirement for the registration of any person with relevant expertise by the Corporate Affairs Commission and other relevant Regulatory Institutions.

regs.title: Administrative penalty.
regs.text: 168. —(1) Notwithstanding the penalties provided under the Act or any other law, any person who contravenes the provisions of these Regulations is liable to an administrative penalty of not less than N 500,000. (2) Any company, government institution or body corporate that contravenes the provisions of these Regulations is liable to an administrative penalty of not less than N 2,000,000. (3) The Commission may by guidelines prescribe a scale of fees for services rendered under these Regulations. (4) Fees chargeable and administrative penalties payable under these Regulations shall be paid into the Fund established under the Act.

regs.title: Powers to seal off building.
regs.text: 169. —(1) Notwithstanding the provisions of regulation 168 of these Regulations, the Commission, in collaboration with a relevant authority, may seal off a built environment found to be in default of the provisions of these Regulations or the Act. (2) Prior to the exercise of its powers under sub-regulation (1) of this regulation, the Commission shall issue an owner, manager, occupier, or developer of the built environment in default a 90 day notice to regularize the default.

regs.title: Issuance of guidelines.
regs.text: 170. The Commission may, from time to time, issue guidelines or circulars for the implementation of the provisions of these Regulations.

regs.title: Interpretation.
regs.text: 171. In these Regulations— “Act” means Discrimination Against Persons with Disability (Prohibition) Act 2018 ; “Call system” means communication technology that allows persons to send signal or information ; “Commission” means the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities ; “Drinking fountain” means a device or receptacle that produces a stream of water or other liquid drink for people to drink from ; “Mobility Aid” means a device designed to assist walking, including, wheel chair, scooter, guide cane, crutches and any other device used to improve the mobility of people with a mobility disability ; “National Accessibility Compliance Certificate” means the certificate issued by the Commission to a person referred to under regulation 2 of these Regulations upon satisfactory compliance with the provisions of the Act and regulation 165 (4) of these Regulations ; “National Disability Compliance Certificate” means the certificate issued by the Commission to a person referred to under regulation 2 of these Regulations upon satisfactory compliance with the provisions of the Act and regulation 165(4) of these Regulations ; “Passageway” means a long, narrow way, typically having walls either side, that allows access between buildings or to different rooms within a building, and includes a corridor and hallway ; “Pedestrian route” includes walkway, pathway ; “Playground” includes picnic area, park ; “Public Building” means buildings used by the public such as hospitals, schools, malls, shops, stores, estates, worship places, fuel stations, hotels & restaurants, offices, recreation and sports centers ; “Two-way communication” means the process of sharing information back and forth between two parties ; and “Wheel chair” includes a motorized wheelchair, scooter, handcycle, etc.

regs.title: Citation.
regs.text: 172. These Regulations may be cited as the Persons with Disabilities (Accessibility) Regulations, 2023.
